(c) *Leave the reset and document it as a self-binding limit* — the app already tamper-detects streak clocks (ADR #31) and treats quota enforcement as its flagship promise; a two-tap bypass is not an acceptable honest limit.

**Verified.** JVM: `rollover_anchorMismatch_seedsFromTheDaysJournal_notAFreshBudget` (row anchored tomorrow + 30 min journaled today → Block, 30 min) and `rollover_timezoneMove_sameDate_preservesJournaledUsage` (5 min journaled + 2 min tick → 7 min, zone re-stamped). Device: AVD `emulator-5554`, over-quota Gmail day; clock forward +1 day (fresh day, allowed), back −1 day (rolls), forward to the original day → the next observation seeds the journal. Evidence and the exact log lines are in `deep-review-2026-10-22.md` (S49-E2-1); full-suite and lint verification is in task #43's record.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A clock change now costs the user nothing on a spent day and cannot manufacture quota; the journal is the sole authority for a day's used time, which is also what Insights and the rebuild path already assume. A tracker row that predates this change and sits below its day total is corrected the next time it rolls; `rebuildProjection` remains the explicit repair for the current row.

## #213 — A Shown Block Wall Re-Bounds Itself on Display Configuration Changes (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented; JVM-verified (`OverlayControllerTest` 20/20) and device-proven on the API-37 AVD (S49-E3-1).

**Context.** Both overlay hosts — the accessibility `Dialog` (`TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`) and the Path B `WindowManager.addView` (`TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY`) — size the window from the bounds passed at show time and do not follow a later display configuration change. During the S49 resilience pass a daily-limit wall was up when the display rotated from landscape (2,400 px) to portrait; the wall kept its 2,400 px width, so only the left slice of the card was visible and the Close button — the wall's only dismissal — sat off-screen. `onConfigurationChanged` existed in `BlockerAccessibilityService` but only logged (and in debug builds only), and the FGS had no hook at all.

**Decision.**

1. **`OverlayController.refreshDisplayBounds()` re-applies the current bounds of every shown card.** For each display with live content it recomputes the geometry from the display metrics (wall = full display bounds, warning = the warning strip) and routes it through the existing per-host `refreshBounds` path, which already handles both the dialog `applyBounds` and the addView `updateViewLayout` mechanisms. The card's content is untouched.
2. **Both hosts call it from `onConfigurationChanged`.** `BlockerAccessibilityService.onConfigurationChanged` (Path A) and a new `EnforcementForegroundService.onConfigurationChanged` (Path B) invoke the controller; the OS delivers the callback to both services on rotation and resolution changes.
3. **`BlockerActivity` is out of scope by design.** The app-block full-screen activity is portrait-locked (C6), so the display cannot rotate while it is the top activity; the fix covers the overlay-hosted daily-limit wall and the Path B card, which do live across rotations.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Listen for display changes inside `OverlayController` via `DisplayManager.DisplayListener`* — duplicate registration lifetime and a second source of truth alongside the service callbacks; the services already receive configuration changes, so one call from each is smaller and testable. (b) *Re-show the card on rotation* — would tear down and re-create the dialog/view and flash the cover; the existing refresh path was built to re-bind without a re-show. (c) *Lock the overlay to portrait* — contradicts the product's rotation support and would strand landscape users.

**Verified.** JVM: `OverlayControllerTest.displayConfigurationChange_reBoundsAShownWallToTheNewOrientation` shows a wall at 2,400×1,080, changes the Robolectric display to portrait via `ShadowDisplayManager`, calls `refreshDisplayBounds()`, and asserts the dialog's width/height/x/y match the portrait metrics. Device: AVD `emulator-5554` with a live daily-limit wall; a genuine system rotation logged `config change: newWidthDp=411` → `display change: rebound display=0 content=DailyLimitBlocked` (00:11:05.727), and the portrait screenshot (`/tmp/s49_rot_gmail.png`) shows the complete card with Close, against the before frame (`/tmp/s49_e3_wall.png`) with text and Close off-screen. Evidence row E3b in `deep-review-2026-10-22.md`.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A wall that is shown while the display is mid-rotation is re-bound on the next configuration callback rather than following the animation frame-by-frame; the user may see one frame of the old layout. Banners are re-bound to the warning strip of the new orientation, which is the same geometry a fresh show would use.

## #214 — Partner-Plan Checks Are Per Local Day; Reads Normalize Yesterday's Ticks (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `PartnerPlanRepository` + `PartnerPlanDao` + `PartnerPlansScreen`; JVM-verified (see Verified) and device-proven on the API-34 AVD (emulator-5556).

**Context.** Owner direction (2026-10-23): a coaching plan is realistically the same steps every day for a week or a month. Once checklist lines can be checked, a check made on Monday must not still read as done on Tuesday — the plan is daily-recurring, not a one-shot list. The shipped model (ADR #193) stored `done` + `done_at_ms` with no day semantics: `done` stayed true forever until the recipient unchecked it or the author edited the line away, so every morning opened with yesterday's ticks and a progress line ("5 of 5 done") that discouraged the day's work.

**Decision.**

1. **Completion is scoped to the local calendar day of `done_at_ms`.** A row whose check predates today's local midnight is yesterday's answer, and a row marked done without a timestamp cannot prove it belongs to today — both count as stale. The boundary is computed with `LocalDate.atStartOfDay(zone)` (not midnight arithmetic) so a DST gap at 00:00 lands on the real day start.
2. **Reads normalize stale rows inside the write transaction.** Both repository reads (`tasks(planId)` and `allTasks()`) clear stale ticks before returning rows. The reset is part of reading, so every consumer — the plans surface, the hub badge, and the sync coordinator's progress payload — sees the same day-scoped state without each one re-implementing the rule.
3. **A paired recipient's reset raises `pending_progress`; nothing else does.** The author's view must learn that the day rolled over, so the reset is published at the next signed sync. An author's display-only copy clears locally without publishing (progress travels recipient → author only), and a self plan never leaves the phone.
4. **The author's copy inherits the day from the event timestamp.** `applyProgress` already stamps each delivered check with the event's `updated_at`, so a progress event that arrives after midnight for a previous day's checks shows unchecked on the author's screen rather than resurrecting yesterday.
5. **The surface re-reads on resume.** A plans screen left composed across midnight would keep yesterday's frame until the next event; an `ON_RESUME` observer (the PartnerScreen convention) re-runs the normalizing read. The plan's detail page explains the rule in one line: "Checks reset each day — this plan starts fresh tomorrow."

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Derive "done today" only at the UI and store nothing* — the sync payload, the hub badge, and the author's copy would each need the same day math, and yesterday's `done` flags would keep flowing on the wire until someone unchecked them; rejected for scattered truth. (b) *Add a cadence column (daily/weekly/once)* — the owner explicitly did not commit to a cadence model and asked for the same plan to repeat daily; a column with one possible value is speculative configuration (KISS). (c) *Carry `done_at_ms` on the wire* — would extend the v1 plan schema for an author-side nicety the receipt timestamp already provides; rejected. (d) *A background midnight job* — the next read is the only moment the answer matters, and a job can be killed or delayed by Doze; read-time normalization is exact.

**Verified.** JVM `PartnerPlanRepositoryTest` (Robolectric, real Room store): a check made today reads done; a check one millisecond before today's local midnight reads unchecked **and the row is cleared**; a paired recipient's reset raises `pendingProgress`; an author's copy and a self plan reset without raising it; `done` with a null timestamp counts as stale; `allTasks()` resets only the stale plan; `localDayStartMillis` maps noon/midnight/just-before-midnight in a fixed zone to the same calendar boundary. Device (API-34 AVD, build of 2026-10-23 15:35): the "Daily" self plan showed `0 of 1 done` with the reset hint; checking "Read" showed `1 of 1 done` with strikethrough; backgrounding the app, setting the clock from Fri Oct 23 15:39 to Sat Oct 24 15:38 EAT, and relaunching (the ON_RESUME normalizing read) showed `0 of 1 done` with an empty box; after restoring the clock (`auto_time=1`, Fri Oct 23 15:39:41 vs host 15:39:43) a further resume still read unchecked, proving the row was cleared rather than the day merely recomputed.

**Consequences / honest limits.** The reset happens when the plans surface is read (screen entry, app resume, partner event) rather than at the exact stroke of midnight; a screen pinned open with the app in the foreground and no resume across midnight is the one stale case, and the first interaction or resume corrects it. Two devices in different time zones reset at their own local midnight — the recipient's next published set is authoritative, which matches how the two copies already converge per revision.

## #215 — The Pairing Wait Outlives the Creator's Clock, and Every Wait Names Whose Phone Owes the Next Tap (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `PairingFlow.awaitPartner` + `PairingCeremonyScreen` + `PartnerScreen`'s EndedCard; JVM-verified (`PairingAdversarialTest` row 11 mutation-proven, `PairingFlowTest`, `PairingFailureCopyTest`) and device-proven on two AVDs.

**Context.** Owner report (2026-10-23): "after we enter the code, the other device doesn't advance its page" — repeated across pairing sessions, and the same confusion occurred to the owner while testing: one side believed the other phone should have advanced while the other was still owed a tap. Two distinct causes. (1) **Clock skew.** `PairingToken.generate` mints `expiresAt` from the creator's wall clock; the Firestore rules compare it to the server clock. The initiator's poll deadline used the same nominal 10-minute TTL measured on the creator's clock, so a fast creator gave up before the server had expired the token. The rig incident: creator clock +3 m 42 s (223 s) — the initiator showed the invitation dead 3 m 42 s early, while a joiner inside that window was accepted server-side. (2) **Silent waits.** Both phones parked on a spinner with no statement of which phone owed the next tap, and the ended state offered no way back into the ceremony.

**Decision.**

1. **The wait carries a skew allowance.** `awaitPartner` polls `timeoutMillis + CLOCK_SKEW_ALLOWANCE_MILLIS` (5 min). The rules' `Denied` — the only clock both devices agree on — is the authority that ends the wait; the allowance only bounds a pathological clock offset. Any other terminal read failure still ends the poll immediately, as before.
2. **The countdown is human-facing copy, never the attempt's stop condition.** It renders "Valid for N more minutes" and then "Expiring now — create a new code if your partner isn't finished."; the screen keeps polling while the server still honours the token.
3. **Every waiting state names the role.** Invite screen: "Waiting for your partner to enter the code…". Joiner after Confirm: "Waiting for your partner to compare the code and tap “They match” on their phone. Keep this screen open." Initiator after its match tap: "Finishing the pairing — this takes a few seconds. Keep both screens open."
4. **A dead invitation is not a corridor.** The Ended partner card carries both ceremony entries ("Invite a partner" / "Join with a code"), wired to the same entry point the hub uses.
5. **The countdown's rounding is pinned.** `PairingFailureCopyTest.invitationCountdownRoundsUpAndStopsAtZero` holds the minutes display honest at the boundary.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *End the wait at the nominal TTL (shipped behavior)* — is the defect; rejected. (b) *Have the server return its remaining TTL each poll and use it for a local deadline* — an extra round-trip that still applies a clock reading to a local timer, while the existing `Denied` poll is already the server's answer; rejected as more machinery for less authority. (c) *Wait indefinitely* — the server's expiry would end it, but a device whose polls permanently fail would never leave the screen; the 5-minute bound keeps the exit honest. (d) *Copy fix alone* — stage guidance prevents confusion but not the stall; both were needed.

**Verified.** JVM: row 11 `fastCreatorClock_partnerRespondingAfterNominalTtl_stillPairs` proven discriminating by mutation (fails against the plain-timeout implementation, passes with the allowance); `PairingFlowTest` 32/0; `PairingFailureCopyTest` 6/0. Device, two AVDs on the same rig: A created the invitation at 15:11:43 with its clock 223 s fast; A's own countdown reached "Expiring now…" while the waiting screen stayed live; B submitted the typed code at T0+660 s (11 minutes — past A's nominal deadline) and was accepted with SAS 51399; A advanced to the SAS comparison roughly 100 s past its own nominal deadline with the same 51399; both phones showed "You're paired" (A paired with SweepB, B paired with AvaA). Stage copy was read on both sides during the waits, and the Ended card's two buttons were confirmed on device.

**Consequences / honest limits.** An initiator more than 5 minutes fast relative to the server still ends its wait before the server expires the token — the bound must exist, and the server may still accept a joiner in that window; the deviation shrinks from "any realistic skew" to "beyond the allowance". The countdown can read "Expiring now" while the screen keeps waiting (by design; the copy points at a possible remedy rather than claiming a state). The allowance is paid on every timed-out attempt (an extra 5 minutes of polling before the error is shown), which is the single cost of not being able to trust either clock.

## #216 — A Cold Signing Window Is Reported, Never Disguised as an Empty Queue; the Foreground Heals It (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `PartnerSyncCoordinator` + `PartnerSyncWorker` + `PartnerSyncSignals` + `MainActivity`; JVM-verified and device-proven on the two-AVD rig (A `rYmVai6KTJbsBn3i7Ld65Zm3kIfQ`, B `aRAqUmAYcCgjjgsfuMCjjQ3AGhv2`, pair `3kS23egEmGkJLUMZ7wWOQTbAui3W_…`, epoch 2).

**Context.** Owner report (#55): partner activity events never appeared on the other phone — no streak, relapse, milestone, message, recovery, coaching or availability event. Root cause, device-proven 2026-10-23: every partner-visible row is signed only during a sync pass, with an AndroidKeyStore key whose 900 s user-authentication window applies; when the window is cold, `emitPayload`/`emitMonitoring` convert `UserNotAuthenticatedException` into a silent `Emit.Stop`, the row stays journaled, and the pass still reported `drained = true`. The periodic worker runs in the background where no prompt may be raised, so a device that booted or sat idle past the window never warmed it — the queue was not empty, it was un-signable, and every caller read the same zero. A second, independent contributor existed in the seed harness: `PartnerActivityDao.pendingForPair`'s v16 consent join requires a `habit_progress_id`, and the old harness wrote rows without one (fixed in the harness; production rows always anchor a habit).

**Decision.**

1. **The pass reports the block.** `SyncReport.signingBlocked` is true when any reconcile queue hit `Emit.Stop` (the coordinator returns `ReconcileOutcome(linked, coldWindow = true)` from every stop site and ORs the flag across pairs). `eventsLinked = 0` is no longer ambiguous between "nothing pending" and "cannot sign".
2. **Background never prompts; the foreground answers.** `runPartnerSyncPass` ticks `PartnerSyncSignals.signingNeeded` when the report is blocked (drop-when-uncollected, like the other repaint signals). `MainActivity.startPartnerSigningHeal()` collects it under `repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)` and calls `healBlockedPartnerSigning()`: run the pass, and only if it is still blocked and the window is cold, raise the user-authenticated prompt (`partner_sync_auth_title` = "Share your updates") and re-run the pass once. A warm window skips the prompt entirely.
3. **Re-prompts are rate-limited; an explicit check is not.** The automatic path asks at most once per `PARTNER_SIGNING_PROMPT_COOLDOWN_MILLIS` (10 min). The Partner page's "Check for updates" (`onPartnerCheckNow`) passes `forcePrompt = true`, bypasses the cooldown, and returns success only when nothing partner-visible remains blocked — the receipt never claims a delivery the device has not made. An in-flight guard makes concurrent triggers (signal + Check now) collapse to one heal; `CancellationException` is rethrown, never swallowed.
4. **Rows stay journaled across a cancelled prompt.** Nothing is deleted on refusal — the next pass, foreground or periodic, retries the same rows. This is the same at-least-once contract the outbox already had; only the reporting changed.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Sign with an always-available key* — the §8.1 pairing contract deliberately binds signing to user presence (NFR4); weakening it would make partner evidence forgeable by anyone holding the device; rejected. (b) *Prompt from the worker* — the system forbids background activity starts for this purpose on modern Android, and a notification-as-prompt would pile another interaction onto a housekeeping job; rejected. (c) *Foreground service with a continuous prompt* — disproportionate, battery-visible, and unnecessary when one foreground pass clears the whole backlog. (d) *Retry with backoff inside the pass* — the window cannot warm without user action; retrying cannot fix it.

**Verified.** JVM (`PartnerSyncCoordinatorTest`): `coldWindow_defersEventCreationButStillDrains` (cold signer → row pending, `signingBlocked = true`, drain still attempted), `warmWindow_reportsNoSigningBlock` (`eventsLinked = 1`, flag false), `activityJournal_coldWindow_leavesTheRowPending`. Device, rig pair above, real keystore, real FCM/mailbox rails: (1) **Streak** — B's cold pass reported `signingBlocked=true` with `pendingForPair=1`, probe cold; the foreground heal raised "Share your updates", PIN accepted, `drain: 1 event(s) delivered`, chain seq=1; A pulled and its Partner page showed "Days free 1 day · Last shared 27m ago" with B pending=0 and a warm signer. (2) **Relapse** — B logged a slip, `drain: 1 event(s)`, chain seq=2; A's page showed "Relapses logged 1". (3) **Milestone** — journey seed (owner-approved harness, one journal row through the production DAO, addressed to the live pair via `-e partnerUid`) delivered day 7, chain seq=3/4; A showed "Days free 7 days, Milestones met 7". The seed harness also exposed and fixed the v16 anchor requirement (rows now seed through the pair's real consented habit, so the SQL consent join matches exactly as production does).

**Consequences / honest limits.** A device whose user never opens the app while rows are queued still delivers nothing — no design can prompt without the user; the partner's page will simply not show new activity until it happens, which is truthful. The heal costs one biometric/PIN prompt per cold backlog, at most once per 10 minutes automatically. `signingBlocked` describes the signer, not the network: a pass can be blocked and still drain earlier, already-signed rows, and it can be unblocked yet fail to upload — the report keeps those separate. The milestone seed is a test harness, not a production path: real milestones still require real elapsed time.

## #217 — Notification Identity Is (Tag, Id) and Tap Identity Is (Request Code, Data); Both Are Scoped per Surface (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `PartnerNotifications` + `StreakNotifications` + `ProtectionNotifications` + `AndroidDomainUsageHost` + `DnsSinkholeVpnService` + new `NotificationTapTarget`; JVM-verified (`PartnerNotificationsTest` 25, `StreakNotificationsTest` 5, `ProtectionNotificationsTest` 2).

**Context.** Owner warning 2026-10-23: "careful with notification channels we dont want collisions." Audit of every post site found three real collision classes and no channel-id collision. (1) **Partner entry ids** were `base + pairId.hashCode()` over consecutive bases 2001–2004: a pair whose hash is 1–3 higher lands exactly on another pair's *next-category* id, and with untagged posts the later category silently replaced the other entry. (2) **Tap identity** — PendingIntent identity is (request code, Intent `filterEquals`), and *extras do not count*. Every partner post shared request code `NOTIF_PARTNER_EVENT` with a bare MainActivity intent under FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT, so a partner-event post rewrote the reach-out nudge's tap and stripped its `TYPE_KEY`/`NUDGE_ID_KEY` routing extras. The same defect existed across surfaces: the protection degraded/outage alerts (Settings) and the VPN-spike and domain-usage alerts (Rules) all used request code 0 with a bare MainActivity intent — whichever posted last rewrote every other notification's tab extra. (3) **Streak milestones** were untagged under a 31-bit stable hash, so two achievements — or a hash and any other surface's fixed id — could evict each other; the "streaks never collide" comment was a hope, not a proof. Channel ids themselves are unique across every surface (`partner_accountability_events_v1`, `approval_requests`, `partner_nudges_v3`, `sync_status`, `availability_alerts_v1`, `checkin_reminders_v1`, `streak_milestones`, `protection_status`, `protection_alerts`, `enhanced_mode_health`, `vpn_spike`, `domain_usage_status`), with retired ids deleted at startup and post paths creating only when missing (the XOS-observed demotion trap documented in the partner code).

**Decision.**

1. **Partner entries are keyed by (tag, id), tag = category + pair.** `partnerTag("event"|"request"|"decision"|"ended", pairId)`; the ids stay (harmless, and existing tests key on them) but uniqueness now comes from the tag. The same category for the same pair still replaces in place — the only case that should.
2. **Streak milestones are tagged and fixed-id.** Tag `streak_milestone:<streakId>:<milestoneDay>`, id 3001. Two habits or two days can never evict each other, regardless of hashes; re-posting the same milestone replaces its own entry.
3. **Every distinct tap target carries its own data URI.** New `NotificationTapTarget` mints `myexodus://notification/<key>` (and `myexodus://habit/<habitId>` for multi-habit surfaces). Data is part of `filterEquals`, so each surface gets its own PendingIntent and extras may differ freely: partner posts key on their tag, streak posts on the habit, protection uses `protection-degraded`/`protection-outage`, domain usage `domain-usage-<id>`, VPN `vpn-spike`.
4. **Channels stay as they are.** They were audited and are distinct; the create-only-if-missing discipline at post time (which prevents the device-observed importance demotion) is unchanged.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Make ids unique by formula only* — any formula over a 32-bit hash can collide; tags make uniqueness structural. (b) *Give every post a unique data URI built from its id* — breaks the intended same-pair replacement (each burst item would become a new PendingIntent, harmless but wasteful) and does not fix entry identity; the NotificationManager side needed its own key. (c) *Per-notification request codes only* — request codes are also 32-bit hashes and a single surface still shares one PendingIntent across its family; data is exact string identity. (d) *Centralize channels in one enum* — cosmetic; there was no channel collision to fix, and the immutability rules differ per channel.

**Verified.** JVM: `PartnerNotificationsTest` 25/25, including a rigged id collision ("BB" hash 2112 and "Ab" hash 2113 — request for one and decision for the other both compute 4015) proving both entries coexist under distinct tags, and `nudgeTapExtras_surviveALaterPartnerEventPost` proving the nudge tap keeps its routing extras after an event post. `StreakNotificationsTest` 5/5 (named copy, three coexisting milestones under one fixed id, re-post replaces in place, habit extra + data URI, denied permission silent). `ProtectionNotificationsTest` 2/2 (degraded tap lands on Settings with its own URI; degraded and outage taps are not `filterEquals`). Full-suite and lint records are in task #43's verification.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A NotificationManager key is (tag, id), so untagged legacy entries posted by a previous build cannot be replaced by the new tagged posts; a package update cancels the app's tray entries, so this is an upgrade-only artifact, not a durable stale-entry path. Tags grow with pair ids (the platform accepts long tags; no length contract is relied on). The data URIs are ours and ignored by MainActivity — an explicit-component intent keeps routing by component, and the app reads only its tab/habit extras.

## #218 — Insights Says Which Days It Covers and What "Time" Counts; a Total Is Never Left to Be Guessed (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `InsightsScreen` + `strings.xml`; JVM-verified (`InsightsRepositoryTest` reconciliation test).

**Context.** Owner report #54: the Insights page's numbers did not reconcile in the owner's reading — Thursday/Friday usage bars of 5m/1m sat beside a 12h 48m trailing total, and "Screen time" reads like whole-device usage. Verified against the code: the read model is internally consistent — `InsightsRepository.load` builds one `daysOut` list (today + the six preceding local days, oldest→newest) and takes `screenTimeTotalMs` as `daysOut.sumOf { creditedMs }` over the *same* rows the strip renders, with `screenTimeTodayMs` as the last row — so the total is exactly the sum of the seven bars, and the discrepancy was in what the screen *said*, not in what it computed: (1) "this week" on the empty lines implied a Mon–Sun calendar week the window never used; (2) the trailing total carried no period label, so it read as a today figure or as a figure covering the two visible bars; (3) "Screen time" claimed whole-device usage, while the ledger's CREDITING rows are written only by `UsageAccountingEngine.processUsageObservation`, whose callers pass only limit-tracked rules — the card is time in apps with a daily limit, nothing else. Website usage lives in the separate `domainusage` tables and never reaches this page.

**Decision.**

1. **The window is stated relationally, never by calendar.** The subtitle and captions say "today and the 6 days before it"; the stat caption says "Last 7 days, ending today"; the three section empties say "in the last 7 days". No copy implies Mon–Sun.
2. **The metered total carries its period.** The usage card's caption is "Total for today and the 6 days before it. Today: %1$s." — the trailing duration is explicitly the seven-day sum, and today's value stays a separate, explicit figure.
3. **The usage card names what it measures.** Title "Time in limited apps"; the "Where the time went" section captions its scope ("Apps with a daily limit, today and the 6 days before it"). The TalkBack bar description says "%2$s in limited apps". The label never claims whole-device screen time again.
4. **The arithmetic stays the single source.** Totals remain sums over the rendered `InsightDay` rows — no second aggregation path was introduced to satisfy a label.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Show whole-device screen time instead* — the app holds no whole-device source; Android's UsageStats aggregates would be a new permission/scope and would count every app, contradicting the ledger's accounting truth (ADR #181); rejected as a different feature with a dishonest name. (b) *Merge website-limit usage into the card* — the domain subsystem keeps its own day ledger, VPN-side metering and rollover semantics; merging is a product decision about what "time" means, not a label fix; deferred honestly (see limits). (c) *Sum only days that have data* — the total would stop matching the bars, which is the confusion being fixed; rejected. (d) *Print the calendar range (e.g. "17–23 Oct")* — accurate but locale-formatted copy that decays the instant the screen stays open across midnight; the relational phrase is stable and needs no formatter and no test clock.

**Verified.** JVM: new `InsightsRepositoryTest.load_usageTotalsReconcileWithTheRenderedBars` — total equals the sum of the seven rendered bars, `screenTimeTodayMs` equals the last bar, a row on the oldest window day counts, and a row one day before the window does not (the exact boundary the old copy made ambiguous). The existing `load_resolvesEveryJournalInOneSnapshot` continues to prove credit-kind filtering (ACCOUNTING + CORRECTION in, HEARTBEAT out) and ADR #210's device render already reconciled strip values with the stat cards on the X6532.

**Consequences / honest limits.** Website-limit time is not on this page at all — the relabeled card no longer implies it is. A user with only website limits sees an honest zero/empty for this section even while a site limit is counting elsewhere; surfacing domain usage on Insights is a future feature, recorded as such rather than papered over by copy. Whole-device screen time remains deliberately unavailable.

## #219 — A Definitive "Service Not Enabled" Shows the Limited Cause Immediately; Only the Listed-But-Not-Yet-Bound Rebind Keeps the Grace Window (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `ProtectionChecks` (`isBlockerAccessibilityEnabled` + `enabledAccessibilityServicesContain`), `BlockingReadiness.accessibilityEnabledByPlatform` (renamed from `accessibilityInEnabledList` by the same-day amendment below), `HomeScreen.pollingOnlySettled` + the polling-only effect; JVM-verified (`DegradationCopyTest.pollingOnly_settlesImmediatelyOnlyWhenTheEnabledListProvesTheServiceCannotBind`, `ProtectionChecksTest` new tests).

**Context.** Owner report 2026-10-23: after re-enabling everything, Home showed "Limited" instead of "Protecting", then flipped a while later — "there's a huge lag … that's bad UX." Device evidence first: on the X6532 after a package update / force-stop, `Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES` was **null**, so the service could never bind; `BlockerAccessibilityService.connected` was legitimately false, authority was legitimately `DEGRADED_POLLING_ONLY`, and `onServiceConnected` → `statusMonitor.refresh()` flipped the chip in ~5 s once the owner re-enabled it. So the chip was never slow — the *explanation* was. Two states were conflated behind one 60 s timer: (a) the service is definitively off (absent from the platform enabled list — nothing will change until the user acts), and (b) the service is listed but XOS has not bound it yet (a real 20–40 s rebind window observed on this device). Only (b) needs patience; withholding the cause card for (a) reads as a lag and hides the action that fixes it.

**Decision.**

1. **The platform state is read as a negative signal only.** `ProtectionChecks.isBlockerAccessibilityEnabled` parses `ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES` (readable without permission; colon-separated `pkg/cls`, short or fully-qualified class via `ComponentName.unflattenFromString`) **and** the `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED` master switch (amendment below; an absent value is not off). `false` proves the service cannot bind; `true` proves nothing about liveness (XOS flaps the listing while the service is alive), so it is never used to *downgrade* a live Path A.
2. **`pollingOnlySettled` is the single pure decision.** The cause card shows immediately (`pollingOnlyPersistent = true`) when authority is `DEGRADED_POLLING_ONLY`, no degradation override applies, and `accessibilityEnabledByPlatform == false`; otherwise the 60 s grace from process start is unchanged. Any other authority or an active degradation settles the card out as before.
3. **The negative signal is not part of `essentialGap`.** `accessibilityEnabledByPlatform` on `BlockingReadiness` is informational; a listing flap on a healthy device cannot flip the chip to LIMITED. Liveness stays `BlockerAccessibilityService.connected`, per the standing rule that the platform enabled list is not a liveness source.
4. **Unknown (`null`) inside the window waits.** A failed settings read must not manufacture an explanation; the state degrades to the old timing.
5. **Grants are re-read on every ON_RESUME.** The readiness read (enabled list, usage access, overlay grant, tunnel) was driven only by the 30 s tick and rule changes, so returning from system settings — the exact moment a user has just fixed a grant — could leave a stale cause card on screen for up to 30 s. A `LifecycleEventEffect(ON_RESUME)` counter now joins the read's keys; the same read, fresh state, immediately.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Drop the 60 s grace entirely* — healthy cold starts would flash a Limited cause card before the service binds, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (b) *Poll the enabled list until the service binds* — the FGS 30 s refresh + `onServiceConnected` already cover the positive path; a poll adds battery cost for a signal that cannot prove liveness. (c) *Use the enabled list as the liveness oracle* — falsified on this device (listing flaps while connected); would reintroduce the false-Limited defect. (d) *Show the card whenever the list is absent, regardless of window* — same as (a) in effect; kept the window for every case the list cannot distinguish.

**Verified.** JVM: the new `DegradationCopyTest` test pins all four branches (false inside window → settled; true inside window → not; null inside window → not; true + window elapsed → settled) plus non-POLLING authorities and every degradation override. `ProtectionChecksTest.enabledAccessibilityList_matchesShortAndFullyQualifiedForms` pins both entry formats and rejects other packages/classes; `isBlockerAccessibilityEnabled_readsThePlatformList` pins the unset→false and full-component→true reads under Robolectric. Device proof on the X6532 recorded in the progress note (disable accessibility with Home open → cause card immediately; re-enable → PROTECTING within seconds).

**Consequences / honest limits.** On a device where the platform list is momentarily absent during a healthy cold start, the card can appear for the first frames and then clear when the service binds — the app cannot distinguish "about to bind" from "off" any better than the setting allows, and choosing to inform immediately when the setting says off is the owner-decided trade. The rebind window itself (listed, not yet bound) still has no card by design; the chip is honest there and flips on bind.

**Amendment 2026-10-23 (same day, after the field was renamed and the master switch was added).** Device evidence while proving #62: XOS clears `Settings.Secure.ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED` to `"0"` after an uncaught service crash **while the enabled list keeps our entry** (captured on the X6532: master `0`, list entry present, `Bound services {}`, then `Crashed services {…}`), so list membership alone claimed "enabled" and the cause card was delayed for exactly the state only the user can fix. `isBlockerAccessibilityEnabled` now returns false when the master switch is explicitly `"0"`; an **absent** value is not off (some OEM builds never write it), which keeps the enabled list as the fallback signal. The readiness field was renamed `accessibilityEnabledByPlatform` to say what it now measures, and `ProtectionChecksTest.isBlockerAccessibilityEnabled_masterSwitchOffWinsOverAListedService` pins the master-switch-wins branch (0 + listed → false; 1 + listed → true). Cold-start re-proof on the X6532 with master `0` and a null list: force-stop → launch, fresh uiautomator dumps at t≈3/7/11 s showed no Home tree yet, t≈18 s showed the "Limited" chip **and** the "Protection is limited / accessibility service isn't running / Re-enable" card together — the card no longer waits out the 60 s window. Restoring master `1` + the list entry rebound the service (`Bound services` present, `authority=FULL`) and the Home chip returned to "Protecting" (screenshot-verified; the concurrent uiautomator trees were stale, the known XOS trap).

## #220 — SOS Recipient Is Chosen per Send from the Live Roster; Never Stored, Never Fanned Out (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `SosConfirmDialog` + `SosViewModel.onTap(message, targetPairId)` + `NudgeRepository.sendNew(..., targetPairId)` + `PartnerDashboardSource.reachOutTargets`; JVM + instrumented tests listed below.

**Context.** Owner 2026-10-23: "we have to configure who gets that SOS, unless you have a better idea." Current behavior already targeted one pair (§19.5: selected when live, else newest; D8), but with N partners the user had no way to choose a different person and the dialog silently assumed the default. The owner's concurrent routing ruling for the partner pillar is **per-subject only** — nothing is shared unless the subject explicitly names a partner, no primary-partner mechanism, no fan-out.

**Decision.**

1. **Pick at send time, from the live roster.** `PartnerDashboardSource.reachOutTargets(selectedPairId)` returns every live enrollment with the §19.5 target first (`displayNameOf` naming grammar, ADR #119). The dialog renders one full-width chip per target **only when N > 1**; a single partner keeps the unchanged one-tap flow with no extra control (ease-of-use rule).
2. **One recipient per send, never fan-out.** Send carries `targetPairId`; `NudgeRepository.sendNew` uses an explicit pick verbatim. A stale pick (unpaired since the dialog opened) is a clean `Unavailable` refusal — the opposite of a silent redirect. There is no stored "SOS partner" preference: the roster is read fresh on each Home entry, so unpairing can never leave a stale target.
3. **Retry identity is the sealed envelope.** An ambiguous outcome retains `(nudgeId, envelope)`; a retry replays it byte-identically and ignores both a message edit and a recipient change — the envelope's AAD already names its pair. Fresh taps (after a terminal result) mint a new identity and honor the new pick.
4. **Widget path unchanged.** The Reach out widget keeps the default resolution; the picker exists where a human is choosing.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Stored "SOS partner" setting* — becomes stale on unpair, adds a configuration surface the owner explicitly did not want, and is redundant with the per-send choice. (b) *Fan-out to all partners* — directly contradicts the per-subject-only ruling; also dilutes urgency. (c) *Dropdown instead of chips* — two taps and a menu for a roster that is usually 2–3; chips make every recipient a single visible tap target. (d) *Ask every time even with one partner* — an unnecessary step in the common case; N=1 has exactly one possible recipient.

**Verified.** JVM: `NudgeRepositoryTest.explicitRecipient_isUsedVerbatim_evenWhenTheDefaultWouldDiffer`, `explicitRecipientThatIsGone_isUnavailable_neverRedirected` (no call, no redirect), `SosViewModelTest.tap_carriesTheDialogsChosenRecipient_notTheDefault`, `tap_carriesTheDialogMessage_andARetryIgnoresAMessageEdit`, `PartnerDashboardSourceTest.reachOutTargets_putsTheTargetFirst_andListsEveryPartnerOnce` (default order, selected moves to front, stale pick degrades to newest, empty/failed read → empty). Instrumented: `NudgeDialogInstrumentedTest` 4 tests — single partner names/prefills/sends edited text, unnamed falls back to the generic title and a cleared field sends null, multi-partner pick updates the title and sends only the chosen pair, cancel dismisses without sending.

**Consequences / honest limits.** With N > 1 the dialog is taller by one label + N chips; that is the explicit cost of not guessing the recipient, and it disappears entirely at N = 1. The chip list is a snapshot from Home entry: a partner added while the dialog is open is not offered until the next entry (and a since-unpaired pick refuses cleanly). Delivery fan-out for state snapshots (ADR #111) is untouched — this decision scopes only the reach-out send.

## #221 — The Identity/Account Transition Inventory Is the Checklist; Anonymous Stays the Default and Every Upgrade Preserves the uid (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Recorded (planning). The inventory is `app/docs/MyExodus Identity & Account Transition.md`; no auth code ships under this decision.

**Context.** Owner request 2026-10-23: once Google or email/password sign-in exists alongside the anonymous default, "certain things in the application need to change, certain structures … need to change"; enumerate them, record them in the relevant documents, and double-check nothing is missed. OPD #6/#30/#36/#37 carry the product context; ADR #125 carries the identity-loss guards.

**Decision.**

1. **Anonymous remains the default; accounts are an optional, uid-preserving upgrade.** Firebase `linkWithCredential` upgrades the anonymous account in place, so pair memberships, mailboxes, push installations and nudges survive. A fresh uid as the "upgrade" path is forbidden.
2. **No uid merging exists.** Signing into an account that already owns pairs, from a device whose anonymous uid owns others, is an explicit choose-one operation with its local-data consequences spelled out — never silent.
3. **Account identity never replaces device-key attestation.** Pair registration and message signing continue to require the server-verified Android Key Attestation chain; account identity is additive.
4. **A new device must re-enroll its attested key.** Signing in restores the uid but not the Keystore keys; the partner-side enrollment names the old signing key, so cross-device recovery needs an explicit re-enrollment rule (partner approval vs trust-on-first-use) and a name-the-person, not name-the-device, presentation.
5. **One identity per install; sign-out wipes local sensitive data after confirmation.** Guest→linked preserves everything (same uid); account switching is destructive by design and never partitioned per uid in Room.
6. **No plaintext behavioral-data egress.** Rules, usage, streaks and recovery stay device-local at runtime; the ruled account benefit is an app-encrypted backup blob (OPD #6, 2026-09-30), which is gated on the still-open key-recovery design.
7. **Account-level deletion is new work.** Only pair-level bilateral deletion exists today; deleting the account must purge pairings (with the partner signal required by Req 24/29), mailboxes, installations, nudges and DMS state, then the auth user — and deregister push so a signed-out device cannot receive the previous account's content.

**Use.** When auth work starts, every numbered item in the inventory (§3 A–I) must be resolved Required / Deferred / Rejected with a reason, the §4 touchpoint map re-audited, and the §7 definition of done satisfied. The inventory's §5 records what explicitly does not change (blocking, VPN, usage accounting, streaks, recovery, widgets, pairing/push/attestation contracts).

## #222 — Reach-Out Notifications Name the Sender; the Push Is Data-Only and the Server Stays Name-Free (2026-10-23)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented in `functions/partner-sos-push.js`, `PartnerNudgePush`, `PartnerMessagingService`, `PartnerNotifications`; deployed (`onNudgeQueueCreated`, `resumePendingNudges`) and device-proven on the X6532 (mapping §5.4).

**Context.** Owner ruling 2026-10-23 (OPD #37 case 1): a notification that says "your partner" is ambiguous when a phone holds several pairs — the copy must name the person. The server stores no names, by design (the pairing label is chosen on the receiving phone), and a hybrid notification+data message is rendered by FCM before any app code runs, so it cannot carry a local name. The plan's §4.6/AD-12/AD-24 specified exactly that hybrid and explicitly forbade the pair id on the wire.

**Decision.**

1. **Data-only, high priority.** `nudgeFcmMessage(tokens, nudgeId, pairId)` sends `{type, nudge_id, pair_id}` with `android.priority=high`, TTL, `restrictedPackageName` — no notification block, no server copy. A missing pair id is omitted (degrades to the generic copy).
2. **The receiving phone names the sender.** `PartnerMessagingService` validates the pair id against the `<uidA>_<uidB>` shape (exactly one underscore, `[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,128}` per side), resolves this phone's pairing label with one bounded (1 s) single-row Room read, and posts via `notifyPartnerNudge(..., partnerName)`. No network, no Firestore, no decryption in the FCM callback.
3. **Generic stays where it belongs.** The lockscreen public version is always the generic copy (FR-13); the named body is unlocked-only; a missing, malformed or unenrolled pair id posts the generic copy with no error.
4. **`pair_id` is relationship metadata, never content.** Both members already see it in Firestore; it reveals that a pairing exists, never what was shared. Names never ride the wire in either direction, and the server never learns a label.
5. **Reliability trade-off, accepted.** A notification block lets FCM render while the app process is dead; data-only processing runs in `onMessageReceived` (high priority wake). A force-stopped app receives nothing and shows the nudge card from Firestore on next open — the card, not the tray entry, is the source of truth.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Server-held display names* — would add PII to the backend, require a DPIA/lock-screen ruling, and leak names the user never consented to share; rejected. (b) *Read the label from Firestore on receipt* — network in the FCM callback, latency, and the label lives on-device anyway; rejected. (c) *Keep generic copy* — the owner explicitly rejected ambiguity with multiple partners. (d) *Hybrid + a second local replacement post* — Android cannot override a system-posted notification; only data-only makes naming possible.

**Verified.** JVM: `PartnerNudgePushTest.validPairId_*` (shape, hostile input), `PartnerNotificationsTest.partnerNudge_namesTheSender_unlocked_lockscreenStaysGeneric`; emulator suite asserts the data-only payload + `pair_id` + the absent-pair degradation; full JVM suite and `npm test` (147) green. Deployed both dispatcher functions. Device leg (§5.4): a real FCM v1 data-only message with a live pair id produced `id=2005 tag=partner_nudge` on `partner_nudges_v3` (importance 4, private) with unlocked text **"Mama reached out — check in when you can."** and the generic public version — the local label was resolved through the production service.

**Consequences / honest limits.** Naming depends on the receiver having an enrollment row for the pair; after an unpair or on a wiped install the copy is generic. An already-posted tray entry keeps the label it was posted with until the next nudge replaces it (fixed FR-19 tag). The full sender→receiver two-phone leg remains hardware-blocked with one physical device; the sender/backend half is covered by the emulator suite and §5.2's earlier two-device proof.

## #223 — Check-In Is Silent: a 45-Minute Server Silence Sends a Data-Only Liveness Probe That Forces a Heartbeat, Never a Notification (owner correction, 2026-10-28)

**Status:** Accepted. Implemented client + server; functions unit **147/147** and DMS emulator **34/34** green; JVM `PartnerSyncCoordinatorTest.forceHeartbeat_ridesThePassIntoCheckIn`, `PartnerPushParserTest`, `PartnerNotificationsTest.deleteLegacyCheckinChannel_removesTheRetiredChannel` green; device leg recorded in the progress note.

**Context.** The owner received a visible "it's been a while since you checked in — open the app" notification while the app was running, and ruled the behavior a bad interpretation of check-in rather than a bug: check-in is MyExodus's own automatic heartbeat, and the user must never be told to open the app so a machine report can flow. The LATE reminder shipped under ADR #203 (fixed generic self-copy, `{v:'1',type:'CHECKIN_REMINDER'}`, NORMAL priority, 45-minute TTL, collapse `checkin`, channel `checkin_reminders_v1`) was aimed at the user even though the thing that was late is a server-side fact — the partner's device had not accepted a beat inside the 45-minute window.

**Decision.**

1. **The visible reminder is retired; the detector stays.** At the same `LATE_AFTER_MS` (45-minute) deadline the worker now sends a **data-only** wake `{v:'1', type:'LIVENESS_PROBE'}`, high priority, `PROBE_TTL_MS` 6 h, collapse key `liveness-probe`, package-restricted — no `notification` block, no server copy, nothing posted anywhere. The same server-side liveness machinery, detection window and outage rebasing are unchanged.
2. **The probe forces the beat the client floor would suppress.** The client's 15-minute heartbeat floor exists to stop cadence abuse, but a server that has gone 45 minutes without a beat is proof its window is stale. `PartnerPushParser` maps the payload to `PartnerPushWake.LivenessProbe`; `PartnerMessagingService` enqueues one unique `PartnerSyncWorker` (KEEP) carrying `forceHeartbeat=true`; `runPartnerSyncPass` forwards it to `PartnerSyncCoordinator.syncOnce(forceHeartbeat)` → `checkIn(force = true)`. Ordinary passes keep `force = false` — pinned by the new JVM test.
3. **At-most-once claim semantics are preserved.** The probe reuses ADR #203's CAS claim (`late_reminder_generation` / `late_reminder_at_ms`, committed before the send, `ALREADY_PROBED` no-ops), so a worker retry cannot stack probes; the field name is retained for schema stability though it now records "probe claimed." The probe is deliberately not routed through `dms_notification_outbox` (no retry machinery, no consent gate): it carries no content, so `pushEligible` must not suppress it — a data-only wake is invisible even when the user turned notices down.
4. **Silence notices to the partner are untouched.** The six-hour partner-facing availability/silence notice keeps its fixed copy, HIGH priority and hashed per-pair collapse (ADR #203). Only the self-directed reminder is deleted.
5. **Upgrades keep no dead channel.** `checkin_reminders_v1` is deleted at startup (`deleteLegacyCheckinChannel`), so system settings never lists a channel that can no longer post.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Soften the reminder copy* — still asks the user to act for a machine heartbeat; rejected. (b) *Force the beat directly in `onMessageReceived`* — network plus crypto in the FCM callback; the worker handoff is the shipped rail (and the existing provider block already defers to it); rejected. (c) *Send the probe through the outbox* — retries the contract forbids and consent revalidation that does not apply to an invisible wake; rejected, same reasoning as ADR #203 (f). (d) *Drop liveness detection entirely and trust the 6-hour notice* — a device whose heartbeats fail at the network edge would surface only as a partner-facing alarm six hours later; the probe is what repairs silence before the partner ever sees it; rejected.

**Verified.** Functions unit 147/147 (`push-payload.test.js` pins the probe as data-only with no notification block; `dms` probe-decision suite pins CAS no-ops, rebasing and the due instant). DMS emulator 34/34 (probe claimed once per generation; outage inside the window rebases; stale/provider/!token skips; `UNREGISTERED` marks the installation stale without a retry loop). JVM: the force flag reaches `checkIn` as `true` on the probe path and `false` on ordinary passes; the parser maps `LIVENESS_PROBE`; the legacy channel deletion is pinned. **Device leg, X6532, 2026-10-28, latest APK via `install -r`:** startup deleted `checkin_reminders_v1` (dumpsys: `mDeleted=true`, deletion timestamp current). A data-only `{v:'1',type:'LIVENESS_PROBE'}` sent through FCM v1 to the live token produced `MyExodusPush: liveness probe — forcing a heartbeat` and ran the forced pass. The first probe landed 13 s after a startup beat and was `RATE_LIMITED` by the server's 30 s abuse floor (`heartbeat-logic.js`); the client resynced 614→615 exactly as designed. A second probe 34 s after the last receipt was **accepted**: `dms_install_state` moved `last_counter` 613→616, `liveness_generation` 441, `last_received_at` 20:45:50Z, `late_deadline_at` rebased to 21:30:50Z. `dumpsys notification` showed only the ongoing `protection_status` FGS row — **no notification was posted**. In its real condition the probe fires ≥45 minutes after the last beat, so it always clears the 30 s floor. Detail in `Obsidian/MyExodus/MyExodus Progress.md`.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A force-stopped or notification-blocked app receives nothing (identical limit to every data-only wake, ADR #222); the next probe after the next deadline repeats, and the 6-hour TTL bounds how stale a queued probe may be. The probe proves reachability, not device health — an offline device answers nothing, and that absence is exactly what the six-hour partner notice exists to report. The field `late_reminder_generation` and the worker log counters `lateDue/lateReminded/lateDeferred/lateStale` keep their names for schema/monitoring stability; their meaning is now "probe" rather than "reminder". A **`RATE_LIMITED` reply is not a failure** — it is the abuse floor working; the forced beat still lands in the real 45-minute scenario. The device leg exposed a log-noise defect: Room `@Upsert` logs a UNIQUE-constraint exception before updating an existing row on every check-in, and the dead full-row `upsertCheckin` could clobber a concurrent writer's columns. Fixed in `PartnerLivenessDao` as `INSERT OR REPLACE` with the dead method removed (rebuilt, reinstalled, heartbeat tests green). **Post-fix APK on the X6532, 2026-10-28 23:55:** a fresh probe was forwarded by the push handler, the forced beat was accepted (`last_counter` 619, `liveness_generation` 443, `last_received_at` 20:55:53Z, `late_deadline_at` rebased to 21:40:53Z), logcat had **zero** `UNIQUE constraint failed: device_liveness` lines through a startup beat, a refusal-resync and the forced beat, and `dumpsys notification` still showed only the ongoing `protection_status` FGS row.

## #224 — The Cloud Functions Error Alert Counts HTTP 5xx Only; Expected 4xx Rejections Are Never Incidents (owner request — permanent fix with proof, 2026-10-28)

**Status:** Accepted. Applied live to policy `projects/myexodus-53804/alertPolicies/7634493270550799513` (Monitoring v3 PATCH, HTTP 200, read-back verified); all prior incidents closed; no open incidents.

**Context.** The owner asked for a permanent fix to the Cloud Functions alert noise, with proof and no guessing. The policy (`MyExodus: Cloud Functions error rate > 5% (15m)`, later AND-ed with a ≥2-error floor, ADR #180-adjacent history in the monitoring doc) counted `cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/execution_count` filtered `status="error"` — and on a gen2 callable **every thrown `HttpsError` is an error execution**: App Check 401 rejections, `RELATIONSHIP_UNAVAILABLE` 403s from a phone whose pair had been removed, and 400 invalid-argument refusals all counted. It produced **56 closed incidents** and no real defect. Seven-day evidence read on 2026-10-28: `submitHeartbeat` 119 error vs 489 ok executions, dominated by 401/403; the `readPartnerStatus` "warnings" were plain Cloud Run 4xx request entries from carrier IPs; the `5xx` series that did exist held 9 requests at 0 s latency with no matching stderr entry — edge transport, never handler code. The metric cannot separate client contract outcomes from server failure, so a threshold change would only mask, not fix.

**Decision.**

1. **One condition, 5xx only.** `resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND metric.type="run.googleapis.com/request_count" AND metric.labels.response_code_class="5xx"`, ALIGN_SUM over 900 s, REDUCE_SUM, `COMPARISON_GT 2` (fires at ≥3 server errors per 15 m), duration 0 s, trigger count 1. Severity ERROR, `autoClose` 1800 s, the existing owner email channel preserved.
2. **4xx is excluded by design, not tuned away.** App Check rejections, relationship denials and validation refusals are the client contract working. They remain visible in CF logs and the dashboard's request-by-response-code tiles; they are not incidents.
3. **The policy's own documentation states the exclusion** so the next operator does not "restore" error-rate semantics by assumption.
4. **No code change was needed for the alert itself** — the fix is the alert's semantics. The 2026-10-21 index-build incidents stay fixed at the source (`functions/index-build-guard.js`, ADR #202); they would no longer page under the new policy either.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Keep `execution_count status=error` and raise the threshold* — expected 401/403 volume is user-driven, not bounded; any threshold is either blind to real failures or pages on client behavior; rejected. (b) *Per-function policies* — multiplies the same signal surface and still cannot classify 4xx inside a callable; rejected. (c) *Alert on log-based ERROR entries* — gen2 handler errors are not reliably emitted as log ERROR with a stable shape, and the existing log metrics are purpose-specific; rejected. (d) *WARNING instead of ERROR* — a 5xx on a callable is a broken feature request, not a warning.

**Verified.** Live PATCH returned HTTP 200 and the read-back matches the intended policy (one 5xx condition, threshold 2/GT, autoClose 1800 s, channel intact, documentation present). The replacement metric carries live data on this project (the 2xx/4xx/5xx series were all observed). No incidents remain open as of the change window; the first real 5xx burst is the first honest page.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A handler that deliberately fails a request with 4xx will never page — accepted, that is a client outcome, not a server defect. A 5xx that originates at the edge/transport (0 s latency, no stderr) still pages once it repeats ≥3 times in 15 m; that is deliberate: it is still a request that got a server error. Monitoring doc §4 item 2 and §5 item 3 were rewritten to this policy on the same day; the old ratio/floor history is recorded as superseded there.

## #225 — The Escalation Plan Is Executed Delta-Only; the Unbuilt Rule-Identity Cluster Is Deferred as the Next Milestone, Not Half-Built (owner ruling, 2026-10-28/29)

**Status:** Recorded (scope decision + audit). The audit itself is plan Appendix D in `app/plans/partner-accountability-escalation-delta-implementation-plan.md`; no new feature code ships under this decision beyond ADR #223/#224.

**Context.** The owner supplied the partner accountability escalation delta plan and ruled **delta-only**: audit every plan requirement against the shipped source, implement genuine gaps, and never rebuild the pairing/crypto/mailbox/outbox/consent/DMS rails that already ship under different protocol choices. The plan's §2/§7 spans both shipped rails and new product behaviour; its own DoD (§17) additionally requires the §12 test matrices and §12.3 device legs before anything is called done.

**Decision.** Every requirement was checked against code, not against other documents, and verdicts recorded in Appendix D (SHIPPED / PARTIAL / GAP / REJECTED / SUPERSEDED). The genuinely unbuilt scope — per-rule partner assignment, rule add/edit/disable/delete lifecycle events, a 5-minute violation-storm summary, backup partner + 24-hour held items, blocked-app uninstall detection, and a daily redacted streak summary — is one product cluster: each item changes the closed event allowlist (ADR #196) and needs UI plus the plan's test matrices and device legs. That cluster is recorded as the **next milestone and explicitly not done**. The parts that conflict with shipped owner-approved decisions are not rebuilt: HPKE/X25519 vs the shipped ECDH P-256 + ECDSA/attestation chain; the Play-first flavor vs the direct-APK channel (ADR #15/#171); signed consent bitmasks vs the shipped per-pair consent flags; the 8 h/20 h DMS cadence vs the owner's 6 h/45 min/24 h policy.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Build the whole delta in one overnight pass* — each gap crosses the closed allowlist, the UI, tests and device legs; a half-built protocol cluster would leave unverifiable states and break the plan's own DoD; rejected. (b) *Declare the plan done on the shipped rails* — the audit proves the headline promises (rule-scoped alerts, uninstall detection) do not exist; rejected as dishonest. (c) *Rebuild the rails to match the plan's protocol* — violates the delta-only ruling and would break the live pair; rejected.

**Verified.** Every verdict in Appendix D carries a code anchor (file/line or ADR). Tonight's actual deliverables are separately device- or backend-proven: the silent liveness probe (ADR #223; X6532 probe accepted, counter 619/generation 443, no notification) and the 5xx-only alert policy (ADR #224; live PATCH + read-back).

**Consequences / honest limits.** The escalation pillar is not complete; the partner-facing promises in the still-unbuilt cluster are unimplemented, and this is stated in the plan, the progress note and memory rather than implied by the shipped pieces. The next plan revision or owner instruction must authorize building that cluster; it consumes the old per-block assignment/streak-routing tasks under the already-ruled per-subject model (OPD #39).

## #226 — Per-Rule Partner Assignment: Pair-Id Roles, Lifecycle Journaled in the Rule's Own Transaction, Routed Only to the Assigned Pair (owner-scheduled milestone, 2026-10-29)

**Status:** Accepted and shipped. This is the rule-identity cluster ADR #225 deferred (plan §2.1 req 1-3, 16, 21-23, §7 M1, §8.4); plan Appendix D rows 1/2/3/16/21/22/23 now read SHIPPED with this anchor, and D.4 lists what still remains (req 4/5 storm, req 14/15 backup, req 17 uninstall, req 18 streak summary).

**Context.** The escalation plan requires every rule to name exactly one assigned partner (optionally a backup and a streak partner), every rule mutation to produce a durable partner-visible event in the same transaction as the write, and rule events to route only to that rule's assigned recipient — while ADR #225 ruled delta-only: never rebuild the shipped pairing, crypto, mailbox, outbox, consent or DMS rails. The shipped app had no rule-to-partner link at all; the rule write path (`RulesRepository`) already used one Room transaction for the rule row + policy version, and `PartnerEventJournal` already provided per-pair routing, retention and event-id idempotency.

**Decision.**

1. **Three nullable pair-id columns on `restriction_rules`** — `assigned_pair_id`, `backup_pair_id`, `streak_pair_id` (schema v21, additive `ALTER`s; the rollback rebuilds the v20 table and drops the new feed). They store **local pair ids**, not the plan's `*_partner_uid`: the enrollment (pair id + verified partner key id + label) is the local trust unit every other partner feature already keys on, and a uid would need a mapping on every read while naming nothing the app can verify.
2. **Cardinality is "at most one", and assignment is optional.** The plan says exactly one; forcing assignment would block creating any rule before a pairing exists, so the editor offers an explicit "No partner" (copy: the rule stays on this device). An unassigned rule journals nothing — there is no eligible recipient. `backup_pair_id`/`streak_pair_id` ship stored but unused until req 14/15/18 are built; nothing renders or routes them today.
3. **Assignment validity is the live roster.** The editor's list is `PartnerDashboardSource.pairRoster()` — the same enrollment read the SOS recipient dialog uses, so only pairs that completed the pairing ceremony (mutual acceptance + attestation-verified keys) can be chosen. No stored 'pending assignment' state exists.
4. **Journaling inside the rule transaction.** `RulesRepository.journalRows` feeds `insertAndBump`/`updateAndBump`/`deleteAndBump`, which already run as Room `@Transaction`: create → `CREATED` to the assigned pair; assignment/unassignment → `ASSIGNED`/`UNASSIGNED` (reassignment writes both, old and new); any other mutation of an assigned rule → `DISABLED` when enabled→disabled, else `UPDATED` — a superset of the plan's "weakening", deliberately not inventing a weakening-specific verb the UI cannot distinguish. `UPDATED` is also what a re-enable writes. Unassigned rules journal nothing. An unrepresentable rule id (legacy non-UUID) or clock (< minute 1) **skips the row, never the write** — the stress suite's pre-1970 finding; a broken clock must not block saving a rule.
5. **Wire contract.** `AccountabilityEventWire` gains kind `RULE_CONTROL` and category `RULE_CHANGED` (schema v1, additive; unknown keys still rejected): body is `event_id`, sequence, rule UUID, one closed verb (`CREATED`, `ASSIGNED`, `UNASSIGNED`, `UPDATED`, `DISABLED`, `DELETED`) and the occurrence minute. No package name, URL, label or free text can ride — the minimizer of ADR #196 is unchanged.
6. **Routing is the route pair, not consent flags.** `PartnerEventJournalDao.dueRuleChangesForPair(pairId, since, now, limit)` is the only reader of rule rows; the coordinator drains it per pair and seals one `RULE_CHANGED` envelope per row (`emitRuleChange`, idempotent via `chain.hasEvent`). The legacy fan-out loop (`dueForDelivery`) filters to `MONITORING_STATUS`, so no path can leak a rule row to another pair. Rule-control delivery is independent of the per-habit activity consent matrix: assigning a partner to a rule **is** the subject's visibility choice for that route (the plan's `RULE_CONTROL` consent row, read under the shipped per-pair consent model — Appendix D row 21 SUPERSEDED, row 22 shipped for rule rows).
7. **Recipient-local feed.** `partner_rule_change` (PK `pair_id` + `event_id`) stores verified rule rows; redelivery is a no-op (`INSERT IGNORE`), expired rows are swept on every insert and hidden by the query, and unpair pruning deletes the orphaned pair's rows. The partner activity feed renders one row per verb ("Created", "Assigned to you", "No longer shared with you", "Updated", "Turned off", "Deleted") — **without** the rule/app name, because the wire carries a UUID and the recipient has no name mapping; naming it would require a new name-exchange feature.
8. **UNSUPERVISED is derived, never stored.** A rule row whose `assigned_pair_id` is not in the live roster shows "Unsupervised — the assigned partner is no longer paired" and stays enforced and visible; the editor shows a "Former partner" row whose only exits are choosing a live partner or "No partner". Unpair never auto-clears or auto-transfers the assignment: a re-pairing mints a new pair id (a new trust unit), and silently promoting a remaining partner to watching rules they were never assigned would be a consent violation.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Store `assigned_partner_uid` as the plan literally states* — needs a uid→pair mapping on every rule read, names nothing this device can verify, and no existing local row stores uids; rejected. (b) *Second outbox/journal table for rule events* — duplicates per-pair routing, retention and idempotency the journal already provides; rejected. (c) *Category-level `RULE_CONTROL` consent toggle* — under the shipped per-pair consent model it would gate a role the partner already accepted at pairing and make an explicit assignment meaningless; rejected as SUPERSEDED by the Appendix D reading. (d) *Auto-clear assignment on unpair* — violates req 23's "remain enforced and visible"; rejected. (e) *Notification for rule changes* — the feed row is the delivery; a push could name no target and would be noise on every edit; deferred until a naming exchange exists. (f) *Free-text rule label on the wire* — violates ADR #196's closed allowlist; rejected.

**Verified.** Stress suite `RuleLifecycleStressTest` (5 tests): 120 rules through the full create→assign→edit→reassign→disable→re-enable→unassign→reassign→delete chain (1,080 writes) produce exactly A=600 rows (`ASSIGNED, UPDATED, UNASSIGNED, ASSIGNED, DELETED` per rule) and B=480 (`ASSIGNED, DISABLED, UPDATED, UNASSIGNED`), all pair-scoped, ascending, UUID rule ids; legacy non-UUID ids store the assignment but journal nothing; 4,500 recipient feed rows insert + full replay keep exactly 1,500 per pair and the top-50 window is newest-first; 2,000 journal rows prove the 30-day retention sweep removes exactly the expired 500 while the 7-day relationship window delivers 1,000; a pre-1970 clock (`minuteOf` = -2) saves the rule and journals zero rows, and resumes journaling when the clock is sane. Receiver tests `RuleControlReceiverTest` (4): verified rule rows become recipient-local feed rows with the right expiry and pair scope, redelivery is a no-op, other kinds are ignored, and the insert path sweeps expired rows. Contract tests pin the `RULE_CONTROL` round-trip and unknown-key rejection; `AppRulesStoreMigrationTest.migration20to21AndBack_addsRuleAssignmentAndFeed` proves the additive v20→v21 upgrade and the rollback rebuild with real Room; dashboard/presentation tests cover the feed row and the `RuleChanged` alert mapping. Full JVM suite: **2,072 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped** (`:app:testDebugUnitTest`, 2026-10-29). Lint: **No issues found** (run alone per ADR #208).

**Device leg (AVD `MyExodus_API37`, then the physical X6532 — see ADR #227):** on the pre-v21 install a website rule (`example.com`) was created through the real UI, then the v21 debug APK was installed with `install -r` over it and the app cold-started: the rule was still listed, its editor rendered the new "Accountability partner" section with the honest empty state ("No partners yet. Pairing happens on the Partner tab."), saving round-tripped, and logcat showed no SQLite/Room exception (only the known emulator Firebase auth/App Check warnings). **On the X6532** the v21 APK was installed over the live database: four real rules survived the migration, the editor's picker listed all six live enrollments, and assigning a rule to "Scenario Partner" persisted across a force-stop cold start (ADR #227). The full pairing-dependent journey (the partner's device receiving the envelope, its feed row, UNSUPERVISED after unpair) cannot be exercised on one device: it needs a second attesting phone (ADR #125), so those legs remain blocked and are recorded as such, not faked.

**Consequences / honest limits.** Per-rule **attempt** routing is not part of this delta: blocked-attempt events still travel the legacy per-pair activity path, so req 16 is shipped for rule-control rows only (consistent with Appendix D row 4 being PARTIAL). The backup/streak columns are inert until req 14/15/18. The recipient feed shows a verb without the rule's identity — by design until a name exchange exists — and the partner UI filters to the last 7 days even though rows persist 30. A rule assigned to a partner who unpairs produces no event to that partner (no eligible recipient) and no event to anyone else; only the owner's UI changes. The pre-1970-clock skip means a device with a broken clock silently journals nothing while still enforcing rules — enforcement is unaffected, and the journal resumes as soon as the clock is representable.

## #227 — The Rule-Journal Work List Advances: Delivered Rows Are Deleted, and the Monitoring Queue Never Sees Rule Rows (owner stress-test finding, 2026-10-29)

**Status:** Accepted and shipped. Corrects ADR #226's delivery mechanics without changing its product decisions; no wire, schema or UI change.

**Context.** ADR #226 routes rule rows through `PartnerEventJournalDao.dueRuleChangesForPair(pairId, since, now, limit)` with `ORDER BY created_at_ms ASC LIMIT 100`. The owner asked for a stress matrix beyond the happy path. The batch-ceiling scenario exposed a starvation defect: a delivered rule row was left in the journal until the 30-day retention sweep, so every pass returned the **same** oldest 100 rows, `emitRuleChange` reported duplicates for all of them (chain idempotency), and rows 101+ were never reached. The same shape existed on the legacy path: `dueForDelivery` had no route-kind predicate, so a pending rule backlog could occupy that query's LIMIT window too — rule rows have no delivery role there, because rule routing is pair-scoped (ADR #226 §8.4 decision 6).

**Decision.**

1. **A delivered rule row is deleted.** After `emitRuleChange` reports `Created` (envelope sealed) or `Duplicate` (already on the chain from an earlier attempt), the row is removed via `deleteById`. `Skip` (cold window / unrepresentable row) leaves it pending for the next pass; `Stop` ends the pass without touching the remaining rows. Delivery is owned by the chain event and its outbox row from creation onward, so the journal row is a work item, not a receipt — deleting it loses no delivery state, and re-running a pass cannot double-send (`chain.hasEvent` plus the unique `(pair_id, sender_key_id, event_id)` index).
2. **`dueForDelivery` excludes routed rows** with `route_pair_id IS NULL`, matching its KDoc contract: the monitoring/activity fan-out and the rule route are disjoint queues, and neither can starve or leak into the other.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Add a `delivered_at` column and filter it* — a second delivery state to keep consistent with the chain and outbox, when the journal already has no delivery authority; rejected. (b) *Raise `RECONCILE_BATCH`* — the same 100 oldest rows would still return every pass; only delays the cliff; rejected. (c) *Order newest-first* — starves the oldest rows instead of the newest; rejected. (d) *Delete only after outbox confirmation* — the coordinator has no outbox read, and the outbox already retries independently; a crash between sealing and deleting leaves the row pending and the duplicate path removes it on the next pass; rejected as redundant state.

**Verified.** Seven new `PartnerSyncCoordinatorTest` tests: one assigned row becomes exactly one chained `RULE_CONTROL` event for that pair only; a row never crosses into another pair; a second pass neither duplicates the chain event nor leaves a work item; a cold-window skip leaves the row pending for the next warm pass; a row created before the pairing moment is not replayed; a 205-row backlog delivers exactly 100/100/5/0 across passes in UUID-creation order (first and last envelopes decoded); and 150 pending rule rows plus one monitoring row yield 101 chain events with every `dueForDelivery` row having `ruleId == null` (no starvation either way). Stress suite `RuleLifecycleStressTest` (5 tests) remains green, including 4,500 receiver rows and the pre-1970 clock skip. Full JVM suite: **2,079 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped** (`:app:testDebugUnitTest`, 2026-10-29).

**Device leg (physical X6532, `DEVICE-SERIAL-REDACTED`, USB):** wireless adb was unreachable from the Mac (phone on LAN-ADDRESS-REDACTED, Mac on LAN-ADDRESS-REDACTED; mDNS resolve also failed), so the leg ran over USB. The v21 debug APK was installed **over the live database** (`adb push` + `pm install -r`; streamed install fails on this ROM): `lastUpdateTime` advanced, Room opened at v21, all four real rules survived, the editor's partner picker listed all six live enrollments, and a rule assigned to "Scenario Partner" persisted through a force-stop cold start with no SQLite/Room exception in logcat. The automatic `partner-sync` worker ran at 14:37 and reported `enrolled=true, uidsResolved=false, eventsLinked=0` (Firebase identity not yet resolvable after the update; Firestore `PERMISSION_DENIED`), so **no rule envelope was sealed on device yet** — envelope creation and drain await the first pass with resolved uids; the partner-receipt half still requires a second attesting device (ADR #125).

**Consequences / honest limits.** Rule rows now vanish from the journal after delivery, so the journal is not an audit log — the encrypted chain and the recipient's feed are. Crash windows are safe in one direction only: a row deleted after sealing is retried by the outbox, while a row left pending after a crash resolves as a duplicate and is then deleted. Retention (30-day sweep) still applies to undelivered rows and to non-rule activity rows.

## #228 — Milestone, Website-Limit and Enhanced-Mode Alerts Banner: Versioned Channels at HIGH (owner report, 2026-10-29)

**Status:** Accepted and shipped. Presentation-only change: no event, schema, or routing change.

**Context.** The owner reported the day-7 milestone notification "did not appear on my screen — it's just in the notification bar", and said the same about other notifications. The check found nothing stuck: the streak was correctly at Day 7 (Home "Days free 7" / "Free since Oct 22", the permanent milestone section ringing the 7 rung, and the widget showing "DAY 7 · 23d to 30-day mark"), and the milestone entry existed in the tray with tag `streak_milestone:<id>:7`, id 3001. The cause was channel importance, read from `dumpsys notification --noredact` on the X6532: `streak_milestones` (3), `domain_usage_status` (3), `enhanced_mode_health` (2) — heads-up needs 4, and the partner channels at 4 demonstrably banner on this ROM (the test alert then available pinned `onHeadsUpPinnedModeChanged`; removed 2026-11-05). Android does not let an app raise an existing channel's importance, which is why the repo's partner channels are already id-versioned.

**Decision.** Milestones, website-limit/VPN-stopped warnings and the enhanced-mode-disabled alert move to new **versioned channel ids at `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`** — `streak_milestones_v2`, `domain_usage_status_v1`, `enhanced_mode_health_v1` — each post path creating the new channel and deleting its legacy id (same pattern as `PartnerNotifications`). The milestone builder's priority is also HIGH. The ongoing protection row stays on `protection_status` (LOW) because it is the persistent foreground-service indicator, and `protection_alerts` was already HIGH; both are unchanged.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Raise the existing channels in place* — the platform silently ignores the new importance for an existing channel; rejected. (b) *Make every channel HIGH* — the ongoing status row is not an alert and a heads-up on every service restart is noise; rejected. (c) *Set only the notification priority* — ignored on O+ whenever a channel exists; rejected.

**Verified.** Robolectric `StreakNotificationsTest` now pins the new channel id and asserts `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` at post time; the affected suites (`streaks`, `blocking`, all `domainusage`) ran **294 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**. `:app:lintDebug` run alone per ADR #208. Device: the important notifications that previously failed this way were enumerated from the live channel dump; channel creation for the three surfaces happens on next post, so a live heads-up shot is owed on the next real warning/milestone.

**Consequences / honest limits.** A new channel id starts with default user settings, so any customization of the old channel is not carried over (the old ids are deleted). Users who muted the old channel will see these alerts again until they mute the new one — that is the intended effect of the owner's report. Nothing was wrong with the streak arithmetic or the widget: cold start did not reset the count, and the Day-7 crossing simply happened after the earlier six-day snapshot.
