**Decision.** `ui/AppLabels.kt` gains `iconCache` (snapshot map keyed `package@sizePx`) and `iconLoads` (in-flight set). `cachedAppIcon()` returns the cached bitmap or null and queues exactly one background load per key on the existing bounded `appLabelLoader` scope; a failed resolution caches nothing and falls back to the placeholder glyph (the honest result for an uninstalled package). `publishLabel` is generalized into `publish(cache, key, value)` so icons reuse ADR #251's snapshot-conflict retry. `AppMark` calls only `cachedAppIcon`.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Keep `remember` and accept it* — rejected: it is still a main-thread binder call per new row. (b) *A size-independent cache* — rejected: call sites render different mark sizes, and caching one decoded size for all would render blurry upscales. (c) *Preload every installed icon at startup* — rejected: unbounded work for targets the user may never see. (d) *Switch `AppMark` to a Coil/AsyncImage dependency* — rejected: the existing loader and snapshot map already do this without a new dependency.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-06).** `AppLabelsTest` adds `iconMissReturnsNullImmediately_thenTheBackgroundLoadPopulatesTheCache` (one resolver call, cache fills) and `concurrentIconMissesForOneTargetQueueExactlyOneLoad` (five simultaneous misses share one in-flight load). Full JVM suite green; Android lint alone clean; `assembleDebug` green.

**Device measurement (X6532, 2026-11-06).** Setup: a 14-app test batch made the Rules page a populated card of labelled rows with real launcher icons; frame stats came from `dumpsys gfxinfo com.example.myexodus` around six injected up/down swipe pairs (`adb shell input swipe`, 350 ms). Cold pass (first scroll after page entry, icon loads landing): 83/85 frames janky (97.65%), p50 97 ms, p90 200 ms, "Slow UI thread" 80. Warm pass (same swipes, cache populated): 90/228 janky (39.47%), p50 17 ms, p90 105 ms, p95 133 ms, "Slow bitmap uploads" 0. Control: the same swipe pattern on the Settings list (no app icons) measured 194/417 janky (46.52%), p50 32 ms, p90 44 ms, high input latency 475. Reading: steady-state Rules scrolling is at or below the no-icon control on jank share and median frame, and no bitmap-upload stalls occur in the scroll; the first pass pays the one-time icon loads. The 90th-percentile tail stayed worse than the control (105 vs 44 ms), consistent with a debug build plus synthetic input (279 high-input-latency frames on the same run), and is stated rather than smoothed over. The test batch was deleted after measurement; no rules were left on the device.

**Other pages (audit 2026-11-06).** Every `AppMark` call site (Home, Rules rows, batch member rows, app picker, Partner alerts, the block screen) now resolves through `cachedAppIcon`; every composition-path label read uses `rememberAppLabel` (ADR #251). The only remaining direct `PackageManager.getApplicationIcon` is `BlockOverlayView.showTarget`, which runs once per block-wall bind, not in a list or per frame. `AppPicker` queries launcher activities on `Dispatchers.IO`; `InstalledApps.launchablePackages` runs one synchronous query when its host first composes and on package add/remove broadcasts, not per row. No other scroll path retains the binder-plus-decode cost.

**Consequences / honest limits.** (1) The first frames of a row show the fallback glyph until the background decode lands, so a fast fling may briefly show placeholders instead of stalling the main thread. (2) The cache is process-wide and grows with distinct `(package, sizePx)` pairs actually rendered, not with scroll passes; it is not evicted. (3) The cold first pass on a freshly opened populated list still janks while icons decode in the background; the main thread no longer issues those calls, but the first paint of each icon is not free.

## #264 — User-Facing Copy Carries No Em Dashes (owner ruling 2026-11-06)

**Status:** Accepted; sweep applied 2026-11-06.

**Context.** The owner asked for em dashes out of the app's copy. Many strings used them as a rhetorical aside in permission, recovery, streak and widget text; three JVM tests pinned the old sentences.

**Decision.** No em dash in any user-facing string. Use a period, colon or comma as the sentence needs. The rule covers `strings.xml`, `strings_recovery.xml` and Kotlin copy literals rendered to users; comments and documentation are unaffected.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Replace every em dash with a spaced hyphen* — rejected: it reads as a typo. (b) *Keep them in long-form disclosure copy* — rejected: the owner's rule is about the app's voice, and the disclosure is user-facing.

**Verified (2026-11-06).** Programmatic parse of both string resource files: zero em dashes in `<string>` and plural `<item>` text outside XML comments. `StreaksPresentation.kt`, `ProtectionScreen.kt`, `CoachingPlanScreen.kt` and `RiskWindowsScreen.kt` literals swept. The three tests that pin exact copy (`WidgetContentTest`, `StreakPluralCopyTest`, `RecoveryDelayCopyTest`) updated and green.

**Consequences.** Copy-only change; no runtime behavior changes.

## #265 — The Milestone Ladder Continues Past 90 Days; Surfaces Show One Stretch at a Time (owner ruling 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented, JVM-verified and linted 2026-11-07; device pass pending.

**Context.** The ladder stopped at 90 days: `MilestoneEvent.MILESTONE_DAYS = listOf(7, 30, 90)`, with the Home grid drawing days 1..90 and the Streaks strip its three rungs. The owner's ruling: after 90 the app keeps counting, marking six months and a year as further rungs, and after a relapse it returns to the original count. The domain detail that shapes the implementation is that milestones are rows, not an enum: `milestone_events` rows are pre-created per streak at onboarding and relapse, and stamping, alarm scheduling, notification claims and backup validation all read existing rows. A display-only change would show rungs that could never be achieved, scheduled or restored.

**Decision.** (1) `MILESTONE_DAYS` becomes `[7, 30, 90, 180, 365]`. (2) The ladder grows lazily: `stampAchievedMilestones` runs `insertMissing(milestoneRows(streakId))` (`INSERT OR IGNORE`) before stamping, so the first evaluation after the upgrade also repairs streaks that predate it and restores from old backups. No schema version change: the table and its `(streak_id, milestone_day)` key are unchanged, and old backups carrying 7/30/90 remain valid. (3) Surfaces show one stretch: days 1..90 (rungs 7/30/90), 91..180 (rung 180), 181..365 (rung 365). `MilestoneWindow`/`milestoneWindow()` in `StreaksPresentation.kt` is the single definition; the Home grid restarts its count at the top left each stretch and rings only that stretch's rungs, the Streaks rung strip shows only that stretch's rungs, and the header keeps the real day count ("Day 120 of 180"; "365 days and counting" past the end). The legend names the current stretch's rungs (singular copy when it has one). A relapse returns to day 1, which lands in the first stretch by construction. (4) `MilestoneReachedDialog` lays its five rungs out `SpaceEvenly` so the full ladder fits. Copy for the two new rungs follows the existing supportive, non-clinical tone.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Keep the grid at 90 cells and add a second row for 91..365* — rejected: it would draw days that do not belong to the current count and contradict the "every cell is a day of this stretch" reading. (b) *A single 365-cell grid* — rejected: 365 cells at 30 columns is 13 rows of unreadable cells, and the stretch-restart is what the owner asked for. (c) *A Room migration to add the two rows to every streak* — unnecessary: the backfill is idempotent and also covers restores, which a migration cannot. (d) *Extend only the display and leave the domain at three rungs* — rejected as above: those rungs could never be stamped or notified.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-07).** Full suite: 2,470 tests, 0 failures. New `evaluate_backfillsRungsTheStreakPredates` deletes all milestone rows (a pre-extension streak or an old restore) and asserts the next evaluation creates 7/30/90/180/365 and stamps only the crossed 7/30/90. `MilestoneSchedulerTest` now pins five alarms at onboarding, relapse, reboot and the long-off-period case. `WidgetContentTest` pins next-rung math past 90. `StreaksPresentationTest` pins window boundaries (1/90/91/180/181/365/400), per-window rungs and the two new headlines. `MilestoneSectionCardTest` (instrumented) still holds at day 5: "Day 5 of 90", legend "7, 30, 90".

**Consequences / honest limits.** A streak that is already past 90 when it is first evaluated after the upgrade will stamp 90 (if unstamped) and 180/365 only when their thresholds are actually crossed; the backfilled rows carry no retroactive achievement, which is the anti-minting rule. Past 365 the final stretch stays on screen with every cell filled and the header reading "365 days and counting"; there is no rung beyond a year in this ruling.

## #266 — Home's Empty and Habitless States Give Direction Instead of Blanks (owner directive 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented 2026-11-07; JVM-verified, linted, and device-verified for the hero and both log-shortcut prompts (the urge path was corrected after the owner's device report, below).

**Context.** Home dead ends: the quick-action dial hid "Log a relapse" when no habit existed and "Reach out" when no live pair existed, so the FAB simply had fewer actions with no explanation; and the days-free hero reserved a 72dp numeral slot that rendered nothing in the no-habit state, leaving a blank band above "No habit tracked yet". The owner asked for guidance at every such dead end and for the empty hero to carry a value that is not zero ("zero implies that you're counting something"). Owner directive 2026-11-07: if a shortcut can appear, it always appears, and a missing prerequisite produces a warning plus the next action instead of a hidden control.

**Decision.** (1) All three dial shortcuts are always present. "Log a relapse" and "Log an urge" open their existing confirmation/sheet with a habit; without one both open the same `Nothing to track yet` prompt, whose body names the write that has nowhere to go and whose **Set up a habit** action runs `beginAddHabit()` and lands on the Streaks setup form. "Reach out" opens the recipient confirmation with a live pair; without one it opens `No partner yet`, whose **Set up a partnership** action lands on the Partner tab (the unpaired hub carries the pairing entry). (2) The empty hero renders **Day 1** (displayMedium, bold, tertiary) in the numeral slot it will later fill: the value the first day will read, not a fabricated count. The caption below still says no habit is tracked and keeps the "Set up a habit" button.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Keep the action hidden and rely on the empty-state CTA* — rejected: the owner's report is exactly that the dial silently lost an action. (b) *Disable the action with a tooltip* — rejected: a disabled greyed row explains less than a dialog and is worse under TalkBack. (c) *Show "0 days" in the empty hero* — rejected by the owner: it reads as a running count. (d) *Show a dash* — rejected earlier (ADR #118 note): a lone glyph reads as glitched content.

**Verified (2026-11-07).** `AppShell` branches on `habit` at each log shortcut's call site and routes both no-habit cases through one `NoHabitPrompt` dialog; Reach out branches on `partnerNames`. JVM suite 2,470 / 0 / 0 / 0. Device pass on the X6532 (release build installed in place, injected taps, rotation guard applied): the dial shows all three shortcuts with no habit and no partner; Log an urge and Log a relapse each show `Nothing to track yet` with their own body; Reach out shows `No partner yet`, and its CTA lands on the Partner tab (unpaired hub with Invite/Join). Lint runs in CI on push (ADR #208).

**Revision 2026-11-07 (owner device report).** The first implementation gated only the relapse shortcut. That was the wrong target: in the build the owner tested, the relapse shortcut was the one hidden without a habit, so the only log action reachable was **Log an urge**, which opened its sheet and wrote a habitless note (`sessions.logOnly`) with nothing to track. The owner's dictated report ("log and add", later "logged and charged") meant the urge action. Both log shortcuts now share the no-habit prompt; the urge body is specific (`There is no habit to log an urge against yet`), and nothing is written without a habit. The same device report added the consistency rule: Reach out no longer hides without a live pair; it shows `No partner yet` and routes to the Partner tab. The Recovery tab's own urge/technique flows are unchanged: they are a standalone V1 feature (Req 10) and are not part of this Home surface.

**Consequences.** A user with no habit or no partner now sees every dial action and is routed to the setup its prerequisite needs rather than reaching a write or send with nothing to target. The prompts reuse `streaks_cancel` and the existing `beginAddHabit()` path, so there is no second setup flow. The one urge row logged before this fix stays in the owner's history; it was not deleted.

**Revision 2026-11-07 (Streaks setup title).** The "Set up a habit" action opened the form titled **"Add another habit"** with no habit in existence, because the title keyed off `onCancel != null` — a proxy for "the FAB opened me" that is true even for a first habit. The title is a fact about the account, not about which button opened the form: `HabitSetupCard` takes `firstHabit: Boolean` and the callsite passes `state == null`; the Cancel button remains keyed on `onCancel`. Observed on the X6532 in the preceding Home unit and queued there; fixed in the Streaks unit, JVM compile green, device re-check recorded with that unit's evidence.

## #267 — The History Page Speaks in Days, and One Entry Can Be Deleted (owner request 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented, JVM-verified, and device-verified 2026-11-07.

**Context.** The owner asked for two things in one unit: remove the single stray urge row written before ADR #266's no-habit gate (a `technique = none`, `STATE_COMPLETED` bare log timestamped 3:30 PM on 2026-11-07), and redesign the History page with the project's UI skills. The deletion constraint is structural, not a preference: the installed build is release-signed, so `run-as` is unavailable, and the store is SQLCipher-encrypted, so no adb-side `sqlite3` can touch the row. The only route to that row is an in-app action. The recovery plan already contemplated one (§5, line 118: "a 'delete recovery data' convenience entry (local recovery tables only, not pairing) is a small W7 add if wanted"), and FR-9's history was the W7 deliverable, so this is the planned small add, scoped per entry rather than in bulk.

**Decision.** (1) **Per-row deletion, session first, links second.** `RecoverySessionDao` gains `deleteById(id)` and `deleteLinksFor(id)`; `RecoverySessionRepository.delete(id)` runs them in that order. `recovery_mirror_link` has no foreign key, so the repository cleans it by hand. The order matters: an orphan link (session gone, link present) is inert, while a missing link on a live session would let the drain deliver the event to that pair a second time. A copy already delivered stays with the partner; nothing retracts it, and the confirm dialog says so in the user's words ("If it was shared with a partner, they keep the copy they already received"). (2) **Paging stays correct after a delete.** The History list's one loader (`load(reset = true)`) runs under the same `Mutex` that serializes "Load more" (the 2026-10-16 finding #16 fix), clears rows/offset/exhausted, and refetches from zero; a stale offset would skip the row that shifts into the deleted one's position. The summary card takes a `refreshKey` that increments after a delete. (3) **One card per local day.** Rows are grouped by `historyDayLabel` (Today / Yesterday / `Sep 25` / `Dec 30, 2025`) into `HistoryDayGroup`s; the day is spoken once as the card heading, each row carries only its local time. The clock, zone, day words and locale are parameters, so midnight, the year boundary and the zone claim are JVM-testable without a clock; the list reads in the device's current zone (travel does not rewrite history). (4) **The summary is a hero, not a chart.** Eyebrow over a Fraunces figure (`headlineLarge`), the range chips always present, one 6dp proportion bar segmented by the three buckets in single-hue alpha steps (primary 1.0 / 0.55 / 0.25 — gold stays reserved for streaks and milestones), and the three legend buckets with swatches. Zeros render in every bucket, an empty period reads "0" in the figure slot plus one explanatory line, and the figure slot never collapses (skeleton while loading, `0` when empty), so switching ranges does not reflow the page. (5) **Loading and empty states are composed.** A skeleton replaces the spinner, sized to the summary card and the first day card; the empty state is an icon plus title plus a one-line hint naming what will appear. (6) The page keeps ADR #80's own `SecureSurface()` and W6's privacy gate.

**Revision 2026-11-07 (owner: "use the ui skills, cause it looks like ai slop").** The first implementation of decisions (3)-(5) was the stock generated dashboard, and the owner rejected it on sight: a rounded card holding eyebrow + giant figure + a 6dp segmented proportion bar + three equal swatch-and-count columns, then one identical rounded card per day, then a third identical card for the empty state — one shape repeated three times, the banned three-equal-columns grid, and a legend that only restated the bar. The revised composition is an unboxed editorial ledger. (a) The summary is a frontispiece: a tracked, uppercase eyebrow with the range as index tabs beside it (colour plus an underline, `Role.Tab` in a `selectableGroup`, every tab keeping its underline slot so switching shifts nothing), the figure in Fraunces `displayLarge` in ink — gold stays reserved for streaks and milestones — a hairline rule, and the breakdown as one prose line ("Completed 4 · Not finished 1 · Logged only 2", `recovery_history_summary_part`). The bar, the swatches, the pill chips and the three-column legend are gone. (b) Day groups are unboxed sections: a tracked day label with a hairline running to the margin, then rows with no card, no accent bar and no dividers; the page's structure is carried by type and rules, not repeated boxes. (c) Dropping the row's accent bar is also a semantic correction: colour was the row's only judgement of its outcome, and the words already say it. (d) The empty state is the summary's zero reading plus one muted hint line; the standalone icon card and the duplicate "No sessions logged yet." title are gone. (e) The skeleton mirrors the new unboxed rhythm. The facts the page reports, the ranges, the three buckets, zeros on every render, the summary's period-only scope and the delete flow are unchanged. Verified: the affected JVM classes (36 tests across `RecoverySessionRepositoryTest`, `HistoryStampTest`, `HistorySummaryTest` and the recovery UI suites) and Android lint (alone, ADR #208) before the device pass below.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Delete the row by adb* — impossible on a release-signed, SQLCipher install; the security posture is working as designed. (b) *Wipe app data or uninstall/reinstall* — refused: the owner authorized exactly one row, and every other session, habit and rule would be destroyed. (c) *A bulk "delete all recovery data" action* — the plan's line allows it, but it does not give the owner a way to remove one entry; per-row deletion is the smaller, more precise affordance, and a bulk action could reuse these DAO calls later. (d) *Link-before-session deletion* — rejected for the duplicate-delivery window above. (e) *Keep the flat list with per-row "Today · 3:42 PM" stamps* — rejected: the reference composition speaks the day once, and a grouped card makes the day boundary visible instead of inferable; ADR #81's summary remains above it. (f) *A per-day bar chart under the chips* — refused for the same reason ADR #76/#79 refused Home and Streaks charts: there is no per-day history to plot, and a chart with one or two rows is noise.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-07).** Full suite: **2,474 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, 266 classes**. `HistoryStampTest` (rewritten, 10 tests) pins Today/Yesterday, the minute-before-midnight boundary, two days back, the year suffix, New Year's Eve still reading Yesterday on New Year's Day, the zone passed in being honoured (22:30 UTC is already the next day at UTC+02:00), the row time in that zone, and grouping that keeps newest-first order both between and inside days while midnight splits the groups. `HistorySummaryTest` (buckets, window boundaries) is unchanged and green. `RecoverySessionRepositoryTest.delete_removesTheRowAndItsMirrorLinks_andLeavesOtherRowsAlone` pins that the row and its link go, the surviving row stays, and a pair that never received the deleted row simply loses it from the queue. Lint and the release build follow this entry; the device pass covering the page and the actual row removal is recorded below once complete.

**Verified (device, X6532, 2026-11-07).** Release build installed in place (`install -r`). The redesigned page rendered its frontispiece (eyebrow, range tabs, figure, prose breakdown) and the day section with the single stray row; the row's overflow menu opened, "Delete entry" raised the confirm dialog ("Delete this entry?", Cancel / Delete), and confirming removed exactly that row: the page then read "0" with "No urges logged in this period." and the empty hint, while Streaks and Home were untouched (Test Habit still 1 day, "Free since Nov 7", milestone countdown intact). The removal was verified through the a11y tree because `screencap` returns 0 bytes on this FLAG_SECURE surface, as recorded below. Rotation guard applied after the injected taps (`accelerometer_rotation=0`, verified).

**Consequences / honest limits.** (1) A deleted session's pending mirror is gone with it: an event that was never delivered to a pair will never be delivered. That is the intended meaning of deleting the entry, and the copy does not promise retraction of copies already received. (2) Deletion is local; the partner's received copy is immutable by design (the same semantics as `RecoveryDataDeleter`'s bilateral protocols). (3) The grouped list reads in the current device zone while each row stores the zone it started in; a travel-time zone change can move a row between day cards, which is the honest reading of "which day is that in my day now". (4) The History surface is privacy-gated and secure, so `screencap` returns 0 bytes by design and the a11y tree is the device verification channel for this page.

## #268 — Urge Rows Carry the Habit They Were Logged Under, and History Moves to Streaks (owner directive 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented, JVM-verified, linted, and device-verified 2026-11-07.

**Context.** The owner asked that logged urges be linked to streaks the same way block attempts are linked to rules, that the link be visible in History, and that History let them switch habits and see that habit's data ("logged urges should be linked to streaks since block attempts are linked to rules..."). Then, before the filter was built, the owner challenged the information architecture: History is retrospective and Streaks is the progress tab (it already carries Insights), so keeping History under the in-the-moment Recovery tab no longer made sense. The owner approved moving it to Streaks.

**Decision.** (1) **Link by habit, not by streak run.** `recovery_session` gains a nullable `habit_id` (schema v25, indexed; `MIGRATION_24_25`/`MIGRATION_25_24`). The habit is the app's switchable unit (the picker's "Your habits", `HabitProgress`); a streak run is never exposed as an addressable object, and a habit's rows must survive its relapses. There is deliberately **no foreign key**: deleting a habit clears the link (`RecoverySessionDao.clearHabitLink` inside `HabitRepository.deleteHabit`'s write transaction) instead of deleting the user's urge record. (2) **Every write path stamps the displayed habit.** Home quick log (`AppShell`), the Recovery tab's log-only and technique sessions (`RecoveryScreen`), and the widget's urge surface (`DesertDawnWidget` intent extra → `WidgetActionActivity` → `WidgetActionViewModel.logUrge(habitId)`) all pass it. The widget's relapse control already carried the bound habit id; the urge control now passes the same id. (3) **History lives under Streaks.** The Recovery hub's History tile is removed (the remaining tiles reflow: techniques + plan, then a full-width crisis path), and the Streaks hub gains a full-width History tile in both the habit and setup states, so a user with no habit can still read rows logged before one existed. The page is hosted outside the hub's vertical scroll because it owns a `LazyColumn`; nesting the two scrollables in one axis is a crash, not a layout. (4) **The filter is the page's own state.** It opens scoped to the displayed habit (`displayedHabitId`), with an "All habits" entry that also reaches unlinked/pre-v25 rows. The control is a tracked eyebrow + current value + chevron under the back row, pinned so switching never needs a scroll; it is hidden when no habit exists, where it could not change anything. Page and summary both filter (`page(limit, offset, habitId)`, `countsByStateSince(fromMs, habitId)`); a filter change resets paging under the existing `Mutex` and holds the skeleton so the previous habit's rows never render under the new label. Under All habits each row leads its detail line with the habit label; under a specific habit the filter already says it. Deleted habits leave their rows unlinked, so they remain under All habits without a label. (5) **Backup round-trips the link.** `LogicalSnapshotCodec` writes `habitId` with `putOpt` and reads it with `optNullableString`, so older backups restore unlinked rather than failing.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Link to the individual streak run (`recovery_streak.streak_id`)* — rejected: no UI ever exposes a past run as a switchable object; the habit is the unit the picker and the hero speak in, and a run-level link would make rows from previous streaks unaddressable after a relapse. (b) *A foreign key with `ON DELETE CASCADE`* — rejected: deleting a habit must not delete the user's urge history. (c) *Non-nullable `habit_id`* — rejected: technique sessions can be run from Recovery before any habit exists, and pre-v25 rows have no link; the column must accept both. (d) *Keep History under Recovery and only add the filter* — rejected by the owner on information architecture (retrospective pages belong with the progress tab). (e) *Two history pages (one global, one per habit)* — rejected: two surfaces showing one log, and no way to say which is authoritative. (f) *A second habit picker inside History* — rejected: the page opens scoped to the displayed habit and the filter is its own narrow scope control; a second full picker would duplicate the global one and imply it changes the displayed habit, which it must not.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-07).** `RecoverySessionRepositoryTest.rowsCarryTheirHabit_andPageAndCountsFilterByIt` pins that `logOnly` and `start` persist the habit, that a null filter returns every row including legacy unlinked ones, that habit filters isolate their rows, and that the summary counts follow the same filter. `AppRulesStoreMigrationTest.migration24to25AndBack_addsTheHabitLink_andKeepsEveryRow` builds a v24 `recovery_session`, upgrades (column present, existing row survives unlinked, value writable), rolls back (column gone, row intact, unrelated table untouched). The existing migration-coverage test requires the pair in `ALL_MIGRATIONS`, which it is. Full suite: **2,476 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, 266 classes** (2,474 before this entry; the two new tests are the ones above). Lint runs alone and is green (ADR #208).

**Verified (device, X6532, 2026-11-07).** Release 1.1.4 (versionCode 6) installed in place (`install -r`). The Streaks hub carries the full-width History tile; opening it lands on the page with the **HABIT** control reading **Test Habit** and the empty-state hint. Logging an urge through Home's quick actions (intensity 6) produced the row in the scoped page: **TODAY · 6:19 PM · Logged, no technique · Intensity 6/10**, summary figure **1** with **Completed 0 · Not finished 0 · Logged only 1**. The Habit control's menu listed **All habits** and **Test Habit**; selecting All habits kept the row and led its details with **Test Habit · Intensity 6/10**, summary unchanged. Back returned to the hub. Honest limit: the setup-state History tile was not exercised on this device because reaching that state would require deleting the owner's only habit; the tile in that branch is code-verified only. The page stays `FLAG_SECURE` and gated, so the a11y tree is the verification channel; rotation guard applied after the injected taps (`accelerometer_rotation=0`, `user_rotation=0`, verified).

**Consequences / honest limits.** (1) A stale widget render can write a row against a just-deleted habit; the row is not lost, it simply appears unlinked under All habits, and the next widget refresh stops offering the stale control. (2) The filter is per page-open: switching the displayed habit on the hub while a History page is already open does not retarget it (the page was opened for a specific log). (3) Rows logged from Recovery while a different habit is displayed carry the displayed habit, because that is the habit the surface was showing; the link is a record of context, not of intent. (4) The History surface remains private and `FLAG_SECURE`; device verification is through the a11y tree.

## #269 — Right Now Is the Recovery Hub's Primary Door: a Local-Only Assist Row, a Deterministic Action Engine, and a Verified Help Directory (owner-approved plan, 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented, JVM-verified, and reviewed 2026-11-07. Device verification pending (the owner's X6532 was away during the build).

**Context.** The owner asked for the Recovery tab and every page under it to be fixed for cognitive overload and generated-looking UI ("as you improve the recover page design ux and ui fixing the ai slop using the ui skills do the same for techniques page and subpages my plan and need urget help page basically all pages and subpages under the recovery page note this"), then approved the resulting plan (`app/plans/urge-assist-redesign-and-recovery-system-audit-implementation-plan.md`) with "i trust your judgement", and added one tap from Home ("it can even be included in the FAB in homepage and in the widget"). After the build the owner ordered a review and stress pass: "do a code review, cleanup, and also stress test... ensure this feature is nice and smooth, no lagging, no vulnerability, no issue... The data that needs to be processed, it's processed at the right time and the right place."

**Decision.**
(1) **The in-the-moment flow is one tap, from four doors.** The hub's "Right now" block, the Home action FAB, the home-screen widget control, and the block screen all land directly on `UrgeAssistScreen` (block screen: `EXTRA_OPEN_ASSIST`). Entries are recorded honestly: `HOME` for the FAB, `WIDGET` for the widget (`EXTRA_RECOVERY_ENTRY`), `BLOCK_SCREEN` for the interceptor, `TAB` otherwise. Entry is a log fact, never an inference about intent (plan line 514).
(2) **An assist episode is a local, unmirrored row.** Every started action writes `recovery_session` with `technique = none` plus `category`, `action_id`, and (at the end) `check_in` (schema v26, migrations 25↔26). The partner mirror never sends these rows (`pendingMirror` excludes technique-none rows; an assist-only action must never reach a partner), and the logical backup carries the three columns. History distinguishes an assist row from a bare log by `actionId != null`, and the summary's fourth bucket ("Urge Assist") renders only once the user has one.
(3) **Selection is deterministic and explainable.** `UrgeSelectionEngine.select` filters hard constraints first — category, an explicit can-move "no" (unanswered is never read as cannot move), disliked actions, actions already tried this episode, the partner-dependent message runner without a partner — then orders by helpful-BETTER history, modality variety against the last action, priority, and effort. A category chip or the gambling in-transaction answer re-ranks the open suggestion immediately, with no Continue step; the Quiet chip deliberately never swaps the action, it only disables audio/haptics for the run.
(4) **Check-in branches the episode, not just the row.** BETTER extends once then finishes; SAME extends at most twice, the second escalating; WORSE escalates immediately; SKIPPED finishes. No action repeats inside one episode, and "I can't do that" removes the action and offers a materially different one.
(5) **Get Help is a verified, Kenya-first directory.** `app/assets/crisis_resources.json` holds 18 entries (Kenya first, then global, then US), each with source, last-verified date, hours/cost/eligibility/limitations only when published. Channels open through `tel:`/`smsto:`/`wa.me`/https via `CrisisChannels`, which normalizes to digits but preserves a leading `+` where RFC 3966 expects it (`tel:+254722178177`); `wa.me` takes digits only. `CrisisResourcesReleaseTest` fails the build on a non-https URL, a missing source or date, an unknown kind, or broken Kenya-first ordering. W6 exempts this screen from the PrivacyGate, not from screenshot protection: `CrisisScreen` declares its own `SecureSurface()` (the crisis content includes a user's chosen filter and panic taps), and the instant-open requirement is met by having no gate, timer, or unlock prompt in front of it.
(6) **Preparation lives under Recovery; the in-the-moment surfaces stay ungated.** The coaching plan (read ungated, edit gated), techniques, risk windows, friction timer, and the assist preferences moved out of Settings to the Recovery hub's Prepare section. `RecoveryPrefs` (mobility, disliked actions, quiet, helpful, haptic pacing) is local, optional, resettable, and unreachable by any partner sync.
(7) **The review pass hardened the flow.** A check-in tap is guarded against a double-tap before the row write lands (`answerPending`); each round carries a token so a late insert is abandoned instead of stealing a newer round's row id; `phase` is not saveable because the round and row id are not (a process death restarts on the suggestion instead of an empty runner); "I can't do that" always abandons the row, technique or not; both log sheets close before the write so a second tap cannot write a second row; "Something else" hides when there are no alternates; the disliked list sorts by the visible label; and the screen declares its own `SecureSurface` (caught by `SecureSurfacesTest`, which the targeted run had not covered).

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *Mirror assist rows to the partner* — rejected: an assist action is a private in-the-moment choice, not shared practice; the owner's standing rule is that sensitive data never leaves without an explicit share. (b) *Reuse the technique runner for assist actions* — rejected: the runner is a timed, haptic, multi-step practice; an assist action may be a three-second breath, a message, or a phone call, and its check-in is the record. (c) *Gate the assist flow behind the coaching-plan unlock* — rejected by the owner-approved plan: the in-the-moment door must always open. (d) *Daily buckets in the History summary* — rejected in ADR #263's pass: a day holds 0–3 rows, so a daily chart is noise. (e) *Infer gambling-in-transaction from the chip alone* — rejected: an inference about the present moment is a claim the user did not make; the question is asked and "Not sure" leaves the ranking as it was. (f) *Save `phase` across process death* — rejected after review: the round and row identity cannot be restored, so a restored RUNNING/CHECK_IN renders an empty runner; a fresh start is the honest landing.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-07).** Targeted Recovery/migration/insights suite green; then the full suite is the gate. `UrgeEpisodeTest` pins the four check-in outcomes, the extend-once and same-twice bounds, no-repeat, and cant-do removal; `UrgeSelectionEngineTest` pins every category, the explicit-mobility rule, quiet/disliked/partner/risk/late-night filters, variety, and the log-only fallback; `RecoverySessionRepositoryTest` pins that an assist row keeps category/action/check-in and is never in any pair's mirror queue, that log-only rows are not either, and that a legacy event_sequence row stays excluded; `RecoveryPrefsTest` pins that an unanswered mobility stays null and "Not sure" clears back to it; `CrisisChannelsTest` pins the `+`-preserving tel/sms forms and the digit-only `wa.me` form; `CrisisResourcesReleaseTest` gates the asset; `AppRulesStoreMigrationTest` round-trips 25↔26; `HistorySummaryTest` pins the assist bucket; `SecureSurfacesTest` pins one `SecureSurface` declaration per recovery screen host.

**Honest limits.** (1) The assist flow is UI-bound; no Compose UI-test harness exists in the JVM suite, so the flow's device edge cases (double taps, back mid-run, message-sent check-in) are static-review-fixed, not test-proven. (2) Device legs are pending: the full flow on the X6532, 200% font, TalkBack, dark and light, and a live partner pair on the local rig. (3) `requiresAudio` is set by no catalog action today, so the quiet filter's audio branch is inert; quiet still disables haptics. (4) A no-partner user sees no message action by construction; the escalation panel names the crisis directory instead.

## #270 — Urge Assist Offers the Whole Ranked Catalogue, Not One Action and Two Alternates (owner direction, 2026-11-07)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented and JVM-verified 2026-11-07. Device verification in progress on the API 37 emulator (the owner took the X6532 mid-pass).

**Context.** On the first X6532 device pass the owner rejected the built flow: "what the hell that recovery wont help anyone? i see no things to help with urges i choose right now whats pulling you and it gives me just generic things or one thing? one action simple action that may not even help? i have a whole doc with research and techniques bro the hell?" Then: "Do what you have to do. Just put yourself in that position of an addict with a strong urge, medium urge, or just a simple urge... Do you think you would have been helped? Because currently, at this proceeding, no... I'm also taking my phone with me, so use the emulators." The plan's §F3/H10.3 rule ("Something else" shows at most two alternates) produced exactly the one-or-three-option dead end the owner described.

**Decision.**
(1) **No silent cap.** `UrgeSelectionEngine` returns the full ranked remainder (`alternatives = ordered.drop(1)`; `MAX_ALTERNATIVES` removed). The panel shows the leading action, then the next four ranked options inline as title + one-line explanation rows, then "Show all N options" for the rest. Ranking is helpful history, modality variety, category priority, effort, with one added rule: when the user named a category, that behavior's designed lead is pinned to the front so the specific signal for this moment outranks a stored helpful preference; the preference still takes the first alternate and leads on its own only when no category was named. Without that pin a helpful-scroll preference displaced the named behavior's answer.
(2) **One-tap breathing stays visible.** When paced breathing is not the primary, a full-width "Breathe with me" button starts it immediately; it is removed from the alternate list so nothing appears twice.
(3) **The researched catalogue gaps are filled.** Two guided techniques join the resource catalog: sensory grounding 5-4-3-2-1 (five phases) and ACT defusion (notice, name, let it sit). Six actions join the assist catalog: disconnect the connection (I05), sensory grounding (I12), defusion (I10), gambling reality check on real numbers (I19), shopping deferred-purchase list (I21), and power the device down (I28). All nine per-category priority lists were rewritten to place them by behavior.
(4) **Techniques lead the hub's Prepare section**, ahead of My plan, because practice is the door a person in an urge is most likely to want.

**Deviation from the approved plan.** The plan's two-alternate cap is superseded by this owner direction. Everything else about §F3 selection (filters, ordering, log-only fallback, safety short-circuit) stands.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) *An intensity questionnaire to triage strong/medium/mild urges* — rejected: the research warns against a compulsory questionnaire in the moment, and the owner's ask is breadth, not more questions. (b) *Keeping the two-alternate cap and adding a separate browse screen* — rejected: extra navigation exactly when navigation is expensive. (c) *Uncapping on the engine but showing everything inline* — rejected: 15 rows of choices re-create the choice overload the plan avoided; four inline plus one tap balances visibility against paralysis.

**Verified (JVM, 2026-11-07).** Full unit suite green (**2,528 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, 272 classes**) and `:app:lintDebug` clean, run alone (ADR #208). `UrgeSelectionEngineTest` now pins the uncapped remainder ("the whole eligible catalogue is offered with no silent cap"), the category ranking, and the category-lead precedence over a stored helpful preference; `UrgeSelectionStressTest` (new, deterministic seeds) sweeps 2,688 answer combinations against the hard constraints and walks 1,200 random episode steps, which caught and fixed a drift where a third "same" could push `sameRounds` past `MAX_SAME_ROUNDS` (now clamped); `RecoveryResourceCatalogTest` still pins id uniqueness and risk-window ordering.

**Honest limits.** (1) Device evidence is emulator-only for this revision; the X6532 legs (200% font, TalkBack, live partner pair) were run on the pre-revision build and must be re-run on the next phone window. (2) The catalog content is offline copy, not clinical advice; no efficacy claims are made in any string.

## #271 — Every Block Wall Carries the Recovery Door, and a Zero-Width Measure Can Never Kill the Process (owner reports, 2026-11-08)

**Status:** Accepted; implemented. Crash fix device-verified on the X6532 (PID survived a font-scale change with an empty crash buffer); the daily wall's recovery action device-verified on the X6532 (tap launched MainActivity and the wall lifted). Path B's wiring is JVM-verified.

**Context.** Two owner reports, verbatim: "why is it some block screens dont hav ethet open My exodus recovery button? and what was that just now when u opened adobe it opened briefly then block screna a ppeard the it glitched app opened again the pause screen stayed". Logcat root-caused both. (1) The "glitch" was a process crash: `IllegalArgumentException: Cannot coerce value to an empty range: maximum -77.0 is less than minimum 77.0` at `NotchedNavBar.kt`, thrown by `coerceIn(min, max)` when a recreation-time measure passed `maxWidth = 0`. The crash killed the process, and with it `BlockerAccessibilityService` and `EnforcementForegroundService`, so blocks silently lifted for the 30–40 s until the system restarted both services — the "app opened again" half of the report. (2) The daily-limit wall was the one everyday block surface with no way into recovery: `DailyLimitBlocked` forced the recovery button GONE, leaving only Close on Path A and, on Path B, no action at all.

**Decision.**
(1) **The notch geometry tolerates a degenerate measure.** `clampToRange(value, min, max)` clamps to `coerceIn(min, maxOf(min, max))`; both `buildBarPath` and the nav-bar composition use it, so a transient zero-width measure lands on the lower bound instead of throwing. A process death must never be the outcome of a layout pass: losing the process takes both blocker services with it, which is a silent protection failure, not a cosmetic glitch. `NotchedNavBarGeometryTest` pins both the degenerate and the normal case.
(2) **The daily wall carries the same recovery action the app wall does.** `OverlayContent.DailyLimitBlocked` gains a nullable `ruleId`; the accessibility host (Path A) reads it from the live rules snapshot and the wall shows "Open MyExodus Recovery". The action starts the friction session and lands on Urge Assist through the same `openRecovery` entry the app wall uses. Without a known rule id (the delete race, or the accessibility-off fallback) the wall stays action-free rather than offering a dead button.
(3) **Path B's degraded wall gets the same door.** `EnforcementForegroundService` injects `RecoveryStateStore`, passes `onOpenRecovery = ::openRecovery`, and passes the rule id into the wall content. This is the only wall a user can face with no accessibility service behind it — the moment the recovery door matters most — and the `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` appop the wall itself requires is a documented background-activity-start exemption, so the launch is permitted. Close still does not appear there: that host cannot evict, and an in-place dismiss would hand the blocked app straight back (ADR #31 / owner ruling 2026-10-03).

**Rejected.** (a) *Hiding the notch bar when the measure is degenerate* — the fix is one clamp, not a visibility policy; a hidden nav bar would flicker and lose the shape. (b) *Leaving Path B's wall action-free because it is "only" the degraded fallback* — rejected: degraded mode is exactly when a user has no other route into the app. (c) *A Close on Path B's wall* — rejected: no eviction token, so Close would just reveal the blocked app. (d) *Giving the delete-race walls a stale rule id* — rejected: the rule no longer exists; a button that starts a session for a dead rule is a lie.

**Verified.** JVM: full suite green. `NotchedNavBarGeometryTest` (degenerate and normal measures), `BlockOverlayViewTest.dailyLimitBlock_withItsRule_offersTheSameRecoveryAction` (button visible, carries the rule id, fires `onOpenRecovery`), and the existing no-rule/Close-survival cases still green. Device (X6532): the font-scale change no longer kills the process; launching an over-budget app showed the wall, and tapping the recovery button launched MainActivity with the Recovery tab, its block banner cleared by the session.

**Honest limits.** (1) Path B's wall was not exercised on-device this pass because it renders only while protection authority is `DEGRADED_POLLING_ONLY`; the wiring mirrors Path A's device-proven entry, and the BAL exemption is verified against the official background-starts documentation. (2) The recovery button's position is geometry-driven; the device tap was computed from a Robolectric measure at the phone's exact display configuration, not from a screenshot (the wall is `FLAG_SECURE` by design).
